articleTitle: Wavefield Characterization of Lamb Wave Propagation in Composite Plates Based on Guided Wave Omnidirectional Wavenumber Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: With the growing application of composite materials in sectors such as aerospace, automotive, and wind energy, accurately assessing their mechanical properties is critical for effective non-destructive testing (NDT) and structural health monitoring (SHM). In this paper, a three-dimensional finite element model was developed to generate the fundamental A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> Lamb wave mode within an 8-layer orthotropic laminate, addressing the complexities associated with the anisotropic behavior of composites. Utilizing the Legendre Orthogonal Polynomial Expansion (LOPE) method, we characterized the wave number profile, revealing significant directional dependence in wave propagation across multilayer laminates. The results demonstrated strong agreement between the analytical predictions from the LOPE method and the finite element simulations, confirming the robustness of our modeling approach. Additionally, we introduced an innovative omnidirectional wavefield representation method, effectively mitigating the influence of phase and group velocity steering angles. These findings enhance our understanding of guided wave dynamics in composite materials, offering valuable insights for the development of more effective detection strategies and assessments of structural integrity in complex composite systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Shear Modulus Distribution in Inhomogeneous Medium on Stress Concentration Around Inclusion
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this work, an analytical approach is applied to study the problem of scattering of SH waves by a circular inclusion in an inhomogeneous media. Based on the complex function theory, the Helmholtz equation of this problem, which is the governing equations of the inhomogeneous problem, is derived with an auxiliary function related to the form of the medium. Subsequently, the governing equations are solved to derive the displacement expressions for the incident waves and scattered waves, and the stress expressions within the medium are determined based on the intrinsic model of the problem. The research work in this paper can provide a reference for subsequent research work on complex inhomogeneous forms.

articleTitle: Dynamic response analysis method for cracked layered nanocomposite piezoelectric-fiber laminated beams carrying moving loads
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this study, the free and forced response analysis method of undamped cracked graphene nanocomposite piezoelectric-fiber laminated (PFL) beams under moving loads are investigated and validated. The beams are regarded as multi-section beams satisfying the Euler-Bernoulli beam hypothesis, and the cracks are modeled as rotating springs with cross-sectional elasticity. The modal expansion theory and Newmark method are used to numerically solve the dynamic response PFL beams. Simple clamped boundary conditions are analyzed, and the dynamic response of PFL cantilever cracked beam tips under different moving load speeds is obtained. The numerical results show that the above method play an important role in the free vibration and dynamic response of the PFL cantilever beam, which provides a reliable framework for evaluating the beam’s behavior under dynamic loading conditions..

articleTitle: Utilizing of Conformal Mapping Method In SH Wave Scattering by Different Shape of Cavities In Inhomogeneous Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Stress concentration is a phenomenon which in the under loading continuous medium with geometric defects exist. Different shape of defects induced varying degrees of stress concentration. In this work, dynamic stress concentration induced by different shape of noncircular cavities under SH wave incidence was investigated. The background medium was suggested to be approximately linear inhomogeneous and infinity. The general expressions of wave and stress fields were obtained using complex function method. With the aid of conformal mapping method, the boundary of different cavities were mapped into a unit circle. Then, the boundary condition equation was constructed and the undetermined coefficients were solved. Finally, dynamic stress concentration factor (DSCF) at different shape of cavities were calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Research On Cooling Plate Flow Rate And Structural Optimization In Thermal Management Of Lithium-Ion Battery Packs
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: During high-rate discharge, the rapid temperature rise in lithium-ion battery pack causes premature melting of phase change materials (PCM), significantly affecting their heat absorption performance, making it impossible to continue effectively absorbing the heat generated by the battery pack. This may affect the overall structural stability of the battery pack and reduce its working efficiency. To address this issue, a cooling method is proposed by introducing a cooling plate and adjusting the coolant flow rate to control the maximum temperature and internal temperature difference in a phase change cooling battery pack. This approach helps delay PCM melting and enhance heat absorption. Results show that increasing the coolant flow rate reduces the maximum temperature but increases the temperature difference, leading to potential non-uniform cooling. To address the overall performance degradation of the battery pack and potential safety issues caused by temperature non-uniformity, a structural optimization method based on controlling the flow rate to adjusting the channel width. Through these optimization strategies, not only can the melting rate of phase change materials be slowed down, allowing them to work effectively for longer periods of time in high-temperature environments, but the overall thermal management efficiency of the battery pack can also be significantly improved, enhancing its long-term stability and safety. This cooling scheme is of great significance for improving the heat dissipation effect of the battery pack and enhancing its working performance and service life.

articleTitle: Influence of Roughness and Porosity on Laser Ultrasonic Detection of Defects in Additive Manufactured Metallic Parts
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A finite element model of laser ultrasonic based on thermoelastic excitation mechanism is established, which is used to detect subsurface defects in laser powder bed fusion parts. The propagation characteristics of Rayleigh waves in TC4 with different roughness and porosity, and their interaction with subsurface defects are studied. The influence of excitation-reception distances on the signal-to-noise ratio of Rayleigh wave under roughness and porosity is further analyzed. The simulation results show that the signal-to-noise ratio of Rayleigh wave decreases with the increase of roughness and porosity. The effect of porosity on the Rayleigh wave signal-to-noise ratio is much smaller than that caused by roughness. By decreasing the excitation-reception distance, the scattering and attenuation of Rayleigh wave by roughness and porosity is effectively reduced. This study provides an important reference for the detection of subsurface defects in metal additive manufactured parts with different roughness and porosity using laser ultrasonic technology.

articleTitle: Development of Small High-Reliability Surface-Mount Quartz Crystal Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: With the system to an integrated, modularization and miniaturized development, quartz crystal oscillator small size ,high reliability have becoming increasingly demanding. It is required to develop miniaturized, high-reliability surface-mount quartz crystal oscillator, including the selection of circuit, the design of quartz resonator and chip, as well as packaging structure design of process implementation. Then the design is verified through the production of quartz crystal oscillator samples and testing.

articleTitle: Optimal Control for Nonlinear Vibration of Piezoelectric Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Cables play an important role in civil engineering and aerospace applications. The active control technique of cable using piezoelectric actuators has received extensive research interest. Traditional research overlooks the material nonlinearity under strong electric fields and geometric nonlinearity in cables subjected to large loads. This paper investigates an active control method for piezoelectric cables that accounts for both material and geometric nonlinearities. Utilizing optimal control theory, the vibration control under various operating conditions is analyzed, including multi-mode free vibration, harmonic vibration, and vibration under random load excitation. The results demonstrate that the designed optimal controller can effectively control the nonlinear vibrations of cables under various operating conditions. By considering nonlinear and multi-mode vibrations, this research provides significant insights into the application of piezoelectric actuators in practical engineering.

articleTitle: The Influence of Geometric Structure on Ferroelectric Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Ferroelectrics as a typical nonlinear dielectric material, exhibit high maximum polarization and moderate breakdown strength, making them promising candidates for high-performance energy storage devices. In this work, a phase-field method based on the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) dynamic equations is employed to investigate the impact of geometric structure on energy storage efficiency and density. By applying electric fields E1 and E2 in the x1 and x2 directions of a carefully designed ferroelectric serpentine mesh structure, we obtained P-E hysteresis loops under different parameter conditions. The results demonstrate a significant influence of the geometric structure on energy storage performance. Increasing the θ angle reduces the total stored energy density, while the energy storage efficiency initially increases and then decreases, reaching its maximum at θ = 60 degrees. Increasing the W/L ratio leads to an initial increase followed by a steady state in energy storage efficiency. Increasing the order of the mesh structure causes the total stored energy density to first decrease and then increase, achieving the highest energy storage efficiency at n = 2. The computational results indicate that optimizing the geometric design can achieve better energy storage density and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Method for Measuring Two-Dimensional Stress in Curved Surface Components Using Ultrasonic LCR Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Curved components are widely used in engineering practice, and accurate and non-destructive evaluation of the stress state of curved components is crucial to ensure the safe service of equipment. In view of the relative scarcity of research on the two-dimensional stress measurement of curved components, this paper proposes a two-dimensional stress measurement method based on array ultrasonic LCR waves, analyzes the influence of curvature on stress measurement, and derives an improved two-dimensional stress measurement model for curved components. The proposed method is simulated and verified using COMSOL software. Finally, a two-dimensional stress measurement system for curved components is built, and two-dimensional stress measurement of curved component specimens is performed based on pre-calibrated coefficients. The results show that within the range of 15-60MPa, the measurement standard deviation is less than 1.5MPa. The experimental results confirm that the two-dimensional stress measurement method for curved components proposed in this paper can effectively evaluate the stress state of curved components.

articleTitle: Wave Propagation in Piezoelectric Semiconductor Microbeams Based on Modified Strain Gradient Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this study, the wave propagation in the piezoelectric semiconductor microbeam is investigated. The first-order shear deformation theory is used. The modified strain gradient theory with three material length scale parameters is adopted to capture the size effect of the piezoelectric semiconductor microbeam. The equations of motion of the piezoelectric semiconductor microbeams are derived by using Hamilton’s principle. The numerical examples are carried out and the effects of carrier density, material length scale parameters and external electric voltage on the wave frequency and phase velocity are discussed in detail. This study will be helpful for the design and manufacture of the piezoelectric semiconductor microstructures.

articleTitle: Effect of Non-Wettability of Piezoelectric Atomizer Hole Wall on Particle Size Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this study, we analyzed and experimentally verified the effect of the non-wettability of the inner wall of the tapered hole in a piezoelectric dynamic cone hole atomizer on the atomized droplet size. First, we used capillary model to analyze and explain the forces and pressure on the droplet within the hole, examining the impact of the non-wetting property of the wall on the liquid. Then, by using a contact angle tester, we measured the contact angles of water and diiodomethane on metal sheet coated with non-wetting material. Additionally, we coated these materials on the large end of the metal sheet in the atomizer and applied vibrations to the atomizer, causing the materials to pass through the tapered hole and form a thin layer on the inner wall. Finally, we conducted atomized droplet size measurement experiments. The results show that for atomizer working at the same voltage and frequency, the non-wettability of the inner wall of the tapered hole reduces the particle size of the atomized droplets from 7.736μm to 1.246μm.

articleTitle: Research on Ultrasonic Grinding System with Large Size, Width-Thickness Wheel: Design, Optimization and Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Rotary ultrasonic grinding (RUG) is an effective machining method for hard-brittle materials. However, the harsh resonant conditions and wide grinding layer result in small vibration output, large energy loss and high temperature rise for large grinding wheel vibration. Therefore, a contactless transfer type of RUG for large-size, wide-thick grinding layer was developed, where the vibration direction is parallel to the machined surface for the end grinding. Firstly, the non-destructive acoustic wave method was applied to measure the elastic modulus. The simulation calculation were combined to obtain the modal shape and the vibration trajectory. Finally, the result show that the resonant frequency was 21.82kHz. The horizontal vibration output was 7 μm. The temperature rise was 41.7°C under 5 μm vibration for 1h, It was verified the performance of ultrasonic end grinding with high vibration, horizontal vibration and low temperature rise, which is of great significance to industrial production and grinding exploration.

articleTitle: FBAR performance analysis with flexoelectricity and strain gradient elasticity
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, we employ theoretical analysis and numerical calculations to investigate the impact of flexoelectricity and strain gradient elasticity on FBAR performance at small scales. By establishing the Stroh formalism for the piezoelectric film and electrodes, and employing the matrix method, we derive the final dispersion equation, which is numerically solved using the multidimensional moduli ratio convergence method. Setting the wavenumber to zero and varying the flexoelectric coefficient and material length scale parameter, the effects of flexoelectricity and strain gradient elasticity on the frequency and overall performance of the device are quantitatively analyzed.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Guided Waves-Enabled Gear Meshing Force Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Gear meshing force measurement is a key aspect of gear transmission system condition monitoring, since it directly affects the transmission efficiency and service life. Traditional gear meshing force measurement methods such as vibration, strain and torque analyses have the disadvantages of low measurement accuracy and difficulty in feature extraction. In contrast, ultrasonic guided waves have the advantages of high sensitivity and strong resistance to noise due to its high frequency and multi-mode propagation characteristics, which can measure the gear meshing force more accurately. This paper presented the principle of guided waves-enabled gear meshing force measurement method. The accuracy of the proposed method for mapping the magnitude of the gear meshing force was jointly verified by finite element simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Reflection of Plane Waves in a Nonlocal Functionally Graded Semiconductor with Surface Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this article, a wave reflection problem in a functionally graded semiconductor half space was studied. Considering non-Fourier heat conduction and non-Fick diffusion for carrier density the governing equations incorporating displacement field, temperature field and carrier density field were established. Four sets of quasi-plane waves including carrier density wave(CDW), thermal wave(TW), quasi-transverse(QT) and quasi-longitudinal(QL) wave were derived. For the incidence of QL wave, the plane waves reflection behaviors at the boundary of functionally graded semiconductor half space were discussed incorporating nonlocal and surface effect based on the numerical calculation. The results indicated that the nonlocal had impact on both phase speeds and reflection coefficient, surface effects only affect the reflection coefficient. Among three surface elasticity parameters, the influence of surface density is greater and the surface residual stress has almost no effect on reflection coefficient. The gradient parameters had a significant influence on elastic wave, and the carrier density is temperature sensitive.

articleTitle: Study on the Sensitivity of the Cross-Correlation Function of Target Scattering Fields Based on Ocean Background Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Background noise carries information about the propagation paths in the process. Existing theories suggest that path information can be extracted from background noise. While substantial research has been conducted on seismic background noise on land, there remains a significant demand for studies applied to marine environments. Current simulation research on ocean background noise primarily focuses on two-dimensional planes, with limited attention to three-dimensional spatial simulations. Therefore, this paper approaches the issue from a spatial perspective by setting up a number of randomly distributed point sources emitting Gaussian white noise to obtain acoustic signals at designated receiving points. We compare the cross-correlation functions in two scenarios: with and without the presence of a target. Due to the existence of scattering fields, we observe a significant difference in the cross-correlation functions between the presence and absence of a target. Additionally, as the radial distance between the receiver and the target changes, differences in the cross-correlation functions are also noted.

articleTitle: Experimental Study for Damage Localization in Steel Beams Based on Cross EMI Signatures
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: An experimental study for the identification and localization of damages in the beam-type strictures is conducted based on cross electro-mechanical impedance (EMI) signatures. The rectangular cracks are intentionally introduced into the steel beam specimens as damages for the purpose of structural health monitoring (SHM). The drive-point and group EMI signatures are respectively measured for all four specimens and then the cross EMI admittance can be calculated through proper electric circuit analysis. A hybrid method integrated with the cross EMI signatures and a damage index named the correlation coefficient (CC) is proposed to identify the damage locations. The experimental results show that the cross EMI signatures are very sensitive to the appearance of introduced damages. Furthermore, the proposed SHM technique is very effective and powerful for damage localization in the beam-type structures.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Mems Piezoelectric Hydrophone Based on Flexible Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, three types of AlN film-based piezoelectric hydrophones with the rigid, quasi flexible, and flexible substrates are designed and the performance of them are optimized by using 3D-FEM in COMSOL simulation software. In addition, a systematically investigation is performed to assess the impact of the silicon layer thickness, PI layer thickness and cavity radius on the receiving sensitivity and resonance frequency of the hydrophones. Simulation results show that the receiving sensitivity level of the flexible hydrophone with PI substrate is 7.18 dB higher than that of the rigid hydrophone based on Si substrate, and the receiving performance is improved by 129.0%. In addition, the resonant frequency of the flexible piezoelectric hydrophone is 39.7 kHz, and the resonant frequency of the rigid piezoelectric hydrophone is 40.2 kHz, which is further reduced by 0.5 kHz. Therefore, the ability to pick up low-frequency sound signals underwater is enhanced. These results can provide constructive guidance for improving the performance of flexible hydrophones.

articleTitle: Research on Cooling Technology Based on Resonant Ultrasonic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Ultrasonic heat dissipation technology has the advantages of no noise, no pollution, fast response speed and strong penetration, but the heat dissipation efficiency is relatively low. In this paper, the resonant ultrasonic field is used to improve the energy rate of the acoustic field and explore the application of ultrasonic heat dissipation technology in the cooling of electronic components. A small flat plate heater is used to simulate the electronic components, and the resonant ultrasonic field is used to dissipate the heat. The performance of the ultrasonic radiator based on the resonant acoustic field is analyzed. Experiments show that when the input voltage of ultrasonic transducer is 30Vp-p, the ambient temperature is 25℃, and the sound field gap is an integral multiple of half wavelength, the ultrasonic heat dissipation effect is the best, and the heat source with initial temperature of 100℃ can be cooled to about 54℃ in 20S. At the same time, the experiment further verifies that when the heat source is wrapped in the barbed wire, the ultrasonic wave can penetrate the barbed wire to effectively dissipate the heat source and broaden the application prospect of ultrasonic heat dissipation technology.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Filtering Algorithm on Absolute Stress Measurement of the Steel Member Based on the LCR Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The absolute stress of the steel member is a vital indicator for evaluating the performance of steel structure buildings. However, further research is required to investigate the effect of the filtering algorithms on the accuracy and speed of the absolute stress measurement. We explore median filtering, Savitzky-Golay (SG) filtering, Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filtering and wavelet threshold filtering algorithms and establish a model between the stress and the ultrasound time-of-flight (TOF) theoretically. The stress measurement platform is constructed and the experiment is conducted. There are good linear relationships between the stresses and the TOF differences for different filtering algorithms, and their fitting determination coefficients (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) are all greater than 0.9995. With different filtering algorithms, the stress measurement errors are less than 9.98 MPa. The experimental results indicate that the filtering algorithms have limited effect in detecting the absolute stress of the steel member utilizing the Longitudinal Critically Refracted (LCR) wave.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Nonlinear Ultrasonic Detection of Fatigue Damage in Nickel-Based Alloy
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A nonlinear ultrasonic testing method was proposed to identify the evolution of fatigue damage in nickel-based alloys. First, the nonlinear ultrasonic testing system was built using RAM-5000-SNAP, and a high-precision pressing device was designed to ensure the compression force between the piezoelectric sensor and the specimen. Then, an experimental study on fatigue damage detection of nickel-based alloys was conducted, establishing a curve to evaluate the relationship between nonlinear coefficients and the level of damage. The results showed that the nonlinear coefficient was bilinear with the fatigue degree, when the fatigue level is below 50%, the nonlinear coefficient increases rapidly with the rise in fatigue, when the fatigue level exceeds 50%, the nonlinear coefficient increases slowly at first and then levels off. Finally, a pattern was discovered in which the fatigue damage area inside the nickel-based alloy and the nonlinear coefficient increased with the progression of fatigue by scanning electron microscopy, which revealed the formation and evolution mechanism of fatigue damage in nickel-based alloys. This provided a basis for detecting microstructural damage in nickel-based alloys using nonlinear ultrasound.

articleTitle: Development of a Novel Bidirectional Piezoelectric Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric actuators exhibit unique merits over electromagnetic motors including compact size, rapid response, high force without gear, and immunity to magnetism. However, the limited output power and the characteristic of most piezoelectric actuators that one actuator can only drive one slider limit their application in conventional devices. In this study, a novel compact piezoelectric actuator which can realize the simultaneous motions of two sliders in different directions without gears and other transmission mechanisms is proposed. The actuator possesses two driving feet, which are located at the upper side and the lower side of the actuator, respectively. The directions of elliptical motions generated at the driving feet are the same under the excitation of the required resonance modes, thus the upper driving foot impulses the upper slider movement in one direction and the lower driving foot impels the lower slider motion in the opposite direction. The structure of the actuator is depicted, and its geometric dimensions are presented. Furthermore, the working principle of the proposed actuator is illustrated. At last, a prototype actuator is designed and fabricated to verify the feasibility and validity of the idea. This study is helpful to the design of robot gripper and other automatic systems that require bidirectional motion.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Active Control of Micro-Vibration of Central Rigid Body-Flexible Arm with Driving Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This work studies the micro-vibration of a flexible arm rotating in space driven by a stepper motor and a harmonic reducer, and a piezoelectric patch is pasted at the root of the flexible arm for vibration control. First, based on the working principles of the stepper motor and the harmonic reducer, the theoretical and equivalent dynamic models of both components are derived. The driving mechanism is equivalent to a two-degree-of-freedom spring oscillator system which stepper motor and harmonic reducer are coupled, and the corresponding motion and torque equations are derived. Then, based on the modeling method of the Lagrange equation, the dynamic equation of the central rigid body-flexible cantilever beam system containing a piezoelectric actuator is established. The influence of rotational speed on the motion of the flexible arm is considered, and the control equation of the system is derived. A PID controller is employed to regulate the voltage across the piezoelectric actuator. A vibration control model is developed on the Simulink platform, and the control effectiveness is simulated and analyzed. The simulation results show that the piezoelectric mechanism designed in this study effectively suppresses the vibration of the flexible arm.

articleTitle: Defect Detection in Liquid-Filled Pipelines Using an Arrayed EMAT to Generate Longitudinal Guided Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Achieving non-destructive testing of liquid-filled pipelines is crucial for ensuring pipeline safety. Liquid-filled pipelines exhibit more complex propagation characteristics. This paper presents a propagation model of guided waves using COMSOL to effectively detect ring defects of a specific depth. The theoretical dispersion curve and attenuation coefficient curve of liquid-filled pipelines are obtained and analyzed to understand the guided waves' characteristics. Additionally, an array electromagnetic ultra-sonic transducer (EMAT) is designed based on the magnetostrictive principle. Simulation results demonstrate that the longitudinal guided wave with EMAT can successfully detect annular defects of a specific depth. Experimental comparisons of defects of varying sizes on guided waves validate the effectiveness of the detection method.

articleTitle: The impact of temperature on crack propagation and pore interaction in graphene-wrapped silver nanoplates under Biaxial tension
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study employed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the biaxial tensile mechanical properties of graphene-coated silver nanoplates at various temperatures. Physical atomic models containing pre-fabricated holes and microcracks were used to simulate the biaxial tensile behavior of the silver nanoplates within a temperature range of 100 to 1100 K, under a constant tensile strain rate. The corresponding stress-strain and energy variation curves were obtained and validated against experimental results. The findings indicate that temperature significantly influences the energy and stress maxima of the system. In the presence of a single hole, an increase in temperature leads to intensified atomic motion, an increase in system energy, and a faster approach to the stress maxima, while the fracture strength of the silver nanomaterials decreases. At elevated temperatures, the stress-strain curve flattens, and the energy values become higher.

articleTitle: Optical MEMS Accelerometer Based on Photonic Crystal with Air Defect Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The accelerometer based on photonic crystals has been widely used in various fields in recent years owing to its characteristics of high sensitivity. A one-dimensional optical microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) accelerometer based on photonic crystal with air defect layer is proposed. The optical sensing system of this accelerometer consists of an asymmetric one-dimensional photonic crystal with an air defect layer. The optical sensing system is designed as an asymmetric structure. Linear tuning can be achieved over a large wavelength range within a limited range of defect layer thickness variations. Compared with existing research results, the accelerometer has higher sensitivity, linearity, and reliability. After calculation by finite element method, the functional characteristics of the accelerometer are as follows: an optical sensitivity of 10.6 nm/g, a mechanical sensitivity of 9.61 nm/g, and a linear measurement range of ±25 g. This accelerometer has high resonant frequency and bandwidth. The optimization scheme of the accelerometer provides guidance for the design of a new MEMS accelerometer, which can be applied to fields such as inertial navigation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multifuntional Shape Memory Polymer Skin for Morphing Wings
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Shape memory polymers, showing advantages of variable-stiffness and large deformation, are widely used for flexible skins for morphing wing. However, it’s quite difficult for sensing of their deformation as well as temperature. and external joule heating are always required. In this paper, a novel morphing skin is proposed. The skin is composed of shape memory polymer and liquid metal wires. Micro-tunnels are designed inside the shape memory polymer skin. The liquid metal is then injected into the micro channels in substructure. The liquid metal wires exhibit functions of temperature sensing, strain sensing and Joule heating. The theoretical models are derived, followed by experimental validation.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Flow Field of an Underwater High-Speed Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The complex underwater environment and the development of deep-sea target "stealth" technology put forward higher requirements for the detection technology of high-speed vehicles, so it is important to carry out the study of flow field detection and characteristic analysis. In order to study the characteristics of the flow field around a high-speed vehicle under actual conditions, a numerical calculation model of the high-speed vehicle sailing with a given motion trajectory was established. Based on the finite volume method to simulate the simulation method of detecting underwater high-speed moving targets in actual engineering, the dynamic water pressure time history curves at different speed conditions and monitoring points at different locations were calculated and analyzed. The results show that the attenuation law of underwater flow field at different depths is consistent with the increase of the velocity of high-speed vehicle. At the same depth, the main frequency characteristics of water pressure signal are consistent. With the increase of vehicle speed, the main frequency amplitude increases by 10%~15%. The simulation results use the hydrodynamic information of the flow field to realize the parametric description of the flow field around the underwater target, and provide a new idea for underwater detection technology.

articleTitle: Study on Ice Layer Thickness Inversion and Sound Velocity Measurement Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The thickness of polar ice layers and acoustic velocity have significant applications in climate prediction, geological exploration, and polar engineering safety. Typically, in situ ice layers parameter measurements require drilling ice samples and measuring the speed of sound by directly measuring the thickness of the ice samples and utilizing the acoustic penetration method, which is highly inefficient for large-area observations. This paper proposes a method to invert ice thickness, Young's modulus, and Poisson's ratio using low-frequency guided wave dispersion curves, based on prior research and the actual characteristics of ice layer structures. Furthermore, by utilizing reflected waves from the bottom of the ice layers and applying an α-filter to extract the arrival times of primary reflected longitudinal and transverse wave signals, we calculate the acoustic velocity of the ice layers. The acoustic velocity shows minimal deviation compared to the inversion results. This study provides a theoretical foundation and methodological guidance for in situ measurements of polar ice layer parameters.

articleTitle: Research on the 3D Imaging Method for Ultrasound Phased Array forward-looking imaging in wellbores
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents the fundamental principles of downhole ultrasonic phased array forward imaging and conducts experiments based on this model. To address the complexities of sound propagation paths, Fermat's principle is employed to calculate the phase delays for each array element. The focusing characteristics of the forward imaging transducer are tested and analyzed, and specific strategies for beam scanning and echo data acquisition are provided. After data collection, geometric mapping is used to localize the echo signals in spatial coordinates, and a distance-weighted (DW) interpolation method is applied to achieve three-dimensional reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate that this method effectively captures the shape and surface details of the scanned objects, offering both theoretical and experimental support for the development of downhole three-dimensional forward imaging technology.

articleTitle: Process Optimization Of Airborne PMUTS For A Demonstration Of Mass Production Of Piezoelectric MEMS Acoustic Sensor On 8-Inch SOI Wafer
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The mass production of piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (pMUTs) has long been constrained by the wafer-level inconsistency of device operating frequency variations, which lead to a poor yield for the industrialization of pMUTs. In this paper, the design, fabrication of airborne pMUT are discussed and 8-inch wafer-level frequency variations are recorded accordingly. The pMUTs were fabricated using a silicon on insulator (SOI) process platform, with the manufacturing process optimized in three key areas: reducing the initial bow of the SOI wafer, improving the thickness uniformity of the Si structural layer, and enhancing the consistency of the backside etch.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of In-Plane Longitudinal-Bending Composite Mode Ultrasonic Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In-plane longitudinal-bending composite mode linear ultrasonic motors are extensively used in precision positioning due to their compact structure and the elliptical trajectory motion generated by the stator, which directly drives the rotor for high-precision linear motion. The motion control, however, is highly complex due to multivariable coupling factors during the output process. This paper thoroughly examines the intricate contact process between the stator and rotor, as well as the influence of friction on output characteristics during actual operation. By employing the modal energy method, we derive dynamic equations for the stator, offering a more accurate representation of its vibration behavior. Furthermore, we analyze the friction behavior in the stator-rotor contact model, incorporating this nonlinear dead-zone behavior into the model equations. The contact forces between the rotor and stator are integrated into the dynamic equations, precisely describing the rotor's motion. This approach results in a dynamic model that accurately reflects the performance of standing wave linear ultrasonic motors, which is crucial for enhancing the non-ideal output performance of ultrasonic motor motion systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Reflection and Transmission Characteristics of Functionally Graded Material Plates Under Pre-Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Due to the limitations of manufacturing processes and the differences in material properties, functionally graded material (FGM) plates inevitably develop internal pre-stress. To investigate the influence of pre-stress on the characteristics of ultrasonic wave propagation in FGM plates, this study examines the reflection and transmission coefficients of FGM plates under pre-stress. First, the governing equations of FGM plates under pre-stress are established, and the boundary conditions are coupled to derive the solution method based on Legendre orthogonal polynomials. The accuracy of the method is then analyzed through numerical simulations. Subsequently, the reflection and transmission coefficients of FGM plates under the influence of both horizontal uniform pre-stress and vertical pre-stress are solved. The effects of pre-stress on the reflection and transmission coefficients are analyzed, providing a theoretical basis for the non-destructive ultrasonic testing of mechanical properties of FGM materials.

articleTitle: An Ultrasonic Time-of-Flight Extraction Algorithm based on Blind Source Separation in the Presence of Non-Gaussian Co-Frequency Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Ultrasonic nondestructive stress testing supports the manufacture of precision equipment. Extracting the time-of-flight (TOF) of an ultrasonic echo signal is crucial for stress detection. However, the co-frequency noise, which is inevitably contained in the echo signal, extremely influences the accurate determination of TOF. This work proposes a novel TOF extraction method to address this problem. The proposed method firstly adds high-frequency signal, and a low-frequency signal into the ultrasonic echo signal. Then, the Co-T algorithm is applied to calculate the TOF by evaluating the minimums of the auto-correlation results of the signals, which are separated by independent component analysis algorithm (FastICA). The proposed method is demonstrably superior to the prevailing the Hilbert and the wavelet thresholding algorithms. Experiments verify the Co-T algorithm's efficacy and accuracy in retrieving TOF from signals in co-frequency noise environments.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analysis of Piezoelectric Semiconductor Circular Annuluses
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Within the framework of the state space theory, this paper establishes an exact model for analysis of the multi-field coupling characteristics of a PSC circular annulus. The nonlinear coupling of electric potential and carrier concentration are effectively solved by using the differential quadrature method. Results indicate the influence of nonlinear effect on electric potential and carrier redistribution in comparison with the linear solutions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Vibration Control and Band Gap Tuning of Piezoelectric Metamaterials Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel piezoelectric metamateial beam is proposed for vibration suppression, and the adaptive band gap control of metamaterials is investigated. By manipulating geometric dimensions, material properties, and arrangement, elastic wave propagation within specific frequency ranges can be effectively suppressed. The study explores both passive and active control strategies, notably utilizing piezoelectric materials coupled with feedback and LC transmission control circuits to dynamically adjust band gaps. A dynamic model is derived using the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, and the vibration response and wave propagation are studied by using the spectral element method (SEM). Numerical results demonstrate that the width and location of both Bragg-type and locally resonant band gaps can be tuned by optimizing parameters like feedback control gain. This work provides a comprehensive framework for designing adaptable metamaterials that achieve targeted noise control and vibration attenuation.

articleTitle: A Mode-III Crack with Surface Effect in a Magnetoelectroelastic Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the contribution of surface effect to the anti-plane deformation of a magnetoelectroelastic medium weakened by a crack is investigated. The surface magnetoelectroelasticity is incorporated by using the extended surface/interface model of Gurtin and Murdoch. The mixed boundary value problem of the mode-III crack is formulated by using a continuous distribution of screw dislocations and the dislocations of electric potential and magnetic potential on the crack, and the problem is reduced to solving a system of coupled Cauchy singular integro-differential equations, which can be numerically solved by the decoupling and collocation methods. The results show that the stresses, electric displacements and magnetic induction near the crack tips exhibit the logarithmic singularity when the surface effect is considered. When there is no surface effect on the crack face, the classical square-root singularity of the near crack-tip fields can be observed.

articleTitle: Development of a Large Aperture Fast Steering Mirror Based on Piezoelectric Differential Driving Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: As optical technology advances rapidly, the application areas for fast steering mirror (FSM) are continually expanding, leading to a growing demand for large aperture FSM. In this paper, a large aperture FSM based on piezoelectric differential driving mechanism is proposed for the above demands. Through numerical simulation and optimization, prototype fabrication, and experimental testing, the results show that the proposed FSM has the function of multi-degree-of-freedom precision adjustment and can realize the function of rapid oscillation of the optical axis of the reflector to meet the requirement of precise pointing of a wide range of beams.

articleTitle: Guided Modes of Flexural Waves in a Lego Plate with a Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Flexural waves will generate guided modes if they are affected by a free edge or a structural boundary. These modes have a propagation characteristic similar to Rayleigh waves, that is, they propagate along the boundary and decay in the direction perpendicular to one. In this paper, we numerically observe guided modes of flexural waves in a LEGO plate with a metasurface. The metasurface consists of a cluster of pillars which are considered as resonators. These guided waves propagate along the metasurface and decay in the direction perpendicular to one. Our work offers a simple method to observe guided modes of flexural waves by common LEGO toys instead of metal specimens, which is easier to verify experimentally and thus deepen the understanding of guided waves.

articleTitle: A FEM Analysis Method for Guided Wave Propagation in Bolted Joints Based on Contact Area Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Bolt connections are prone to loosening in harsh working environments. Ultrasonic guided waves can be used for online monitoring of bolt loosening. Accurately analyzing the propagation of ultrasonic guided waves under different bolt preload conditions using finite element method (FEM) is an important means to improve the guided wave monitoring method. However, the current FEM method still has limitations such as long computation time and inaccurate contact surface modeling. This paper proposes a finite element method based on explicit dynamics and contact area measurement. First, the actual contact area at the bolt connection interface is determined using Fuji pressure-sensitive film. Then, an explicit dynamics method is used to establish a finite element model of the bolt connection structure to accurately simulate the connection state under different preload conditions. The model is validated by different bolt loosening monitoring methods. Simulation and experimental results show that the improved time reversal method can improve the sensitivity of bolt preload monitoring, and the conclusions of the finite element method are consistent with the experimental results. The finite element method proposed in this paper can effectively simulate the propagation of guided waves and reduce the calculation cost, with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual-Mode Ultrasonic Probe for Ultrasound-Mediated Microbubble Cavitation Assisted Thrombolysis
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Thrombus poses a significant threat to human health, leading to severe conditions such as myocardial infarction and pulmonary embolism. Ultrasound-mediated microbubble cavitation assisted thrombolysis (UMCAT) is increasingly becoming a mainstream approach for thrombolysis. The efficiency of UMCAT largely depends on the ultrasonic probes used, which are crucial for effective thrombus dissolution. However, current ultrasonic probes for thrombolysis emit ultrasound in only a single direction, severely limiting thrombolysis efficiency. Therefore, developing an ultrasonic probe with broad radiation direction and high energy intensity is essential for improving thrombolysis outcomes. This work proposed a dual-mode ultrasonic probe for thrombolysis. The dual-mode ultrasonic probe features a stacked transducer (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 224.5 kHz) and a cylindrical transducer (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 3.8 MHz), which emit ultrasound in the axial and radial directions, respectively. The dual-mode ultrasonic probe significantly accelerates the process of ultrasound-mediated microbubble cavitation assisted thrombolysis through simultaneously emitting ultrasound in both axial and radial directions. Liposome microbubble with an average diameter of 5 μm was prepared to further enhance cavitation intensity. In-vitro experiments based on the combined effect of ultrasound, microbubble and thrombolytic drug (urokinase) were conducted to validate the UMCAT effectiveness using the proposed dual-mode ultrasonic probe. Results indicated that dual-mode ultrasonic probe significantly enhances the efficiency of ultrasound-mediated microbubble cavitation thrombolysis, outperforming both drug-only thrombolysis and ultrasound-only thrombolysis. The mass reduction of thrombus reaches 54.47% after 20 minutes with the dual-mode probe. These findings demonstrated that the proposed dual-mode ultrasonic probe offers superior thrombolysis efficiency compared to traditional ultrasonic probes, providing theoretical and experimental foundations for interventional ultrasound thrombolysis, holding substantial potential for clinical applications.

articleTitle: Stress Measurement of Shell Structure Sections using New Featured Shear Waves EMATs
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The assessment and surveillance of stress play a crucial role in ensuring the safety, strengthening, and upkeep of steel structures. This paper delves into the field of stress measurement through the utilization of ultrasonic shear wave birefringence. Acoustic birefringence, arising from material anisotropy due to manufacturing textures and loading-induced stresses, refers to the difference in velocity between orthogonally polarized shear waves. Traditional shear wave birefringence techniques are inefficient in performing internal stress of the components. In this study, we proposed a method for measuring stress theoretically and experimentally. Newly designed Electromagnetic Acoustic Transducer (EMAT) was created to measure uniaxial stress. A self-constructed pulser-receiver was also employed in the measurement system to ensure the simultaneous generation of two orthogonally polarized shear waves. Good agreement was obtained with theoretical stress values.

articleTitle: A Study of the Contour Morphology of Dynamic Mesh-Type Ultrasonic Atomizer Sprays
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In the field of atomizers, various parameters have been used to describe atomization characteristics, yet the phenomenon of spray tilt and dispersion is still lacking relevant parameters to describe accurately. Therefore, it is necessary to develop parameters to describe these phenomena in order to provide a theoretical and experimental foundation for future research on spray characteristics. Firstly, a theoretical model of spray was established, and the tilt angle was defining based on spray tilting phenomena, and simultaneously the dispersion angle was defining based on varying degrees of spray dispersion observed in different instances. Further experiments were conducted to validate the theoretical definitions of tilt angle and dispersion angle. Spray contours were photographed, and the obtained spray contour images were processed and analyzed to extract the spray contour. Curve fitting and calculation were performed using theoretical formulas. The calculated tilt angle and dispersion angle were compared with the spray contour images. The experimental results demonstrate that the tilt angle and dispersion angle can serve as parameters to describe the state of spray contours.

articleTitle: Enhanced Design for Low-Frequency Acoustic Absorption in Ultra-Light Porous Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: How to improve the low-frequency sound-absorbing performance of ultra-light porous materials is a highly engineered problem of great value. In this paper, the sound absorption performance of porous material with rigid inclusion is studied from the perspective of forward design and reverse design at the same time. Firstly, a theoretical model of the system's sound absorption performance is established based on the transfer matrix method and the JCA model. Further, a finite element framework for acoustic field problems is established, and the reverse design of the insertion inclusion structure based on density topology optimization method is carried out. The results show that the low-frequency sound absorption performance of porous materials can be significantly enhanced by setting the inserted rigid inclusion structure. The physical mechanism lies in the low frequency resonance achieved by the rigid inclusion, and the energy is still mainly absorbed through the porous material. The reverse design method proposed in this paper provides a powerful design tool for the porous material-insert system.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Contact Areas in Bolted Joints on Guided Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Bolted joints are extensively employed in aerospace, mechanical engineering, and civil engineering applications. Failures in these connections can severely undermine system reliability, making the online monitoring of bolt preload essential for ensuring structural safety. However, the application of the ultrasonic guided wave energy method for detecting bolt preload is complicated by an unclear interaction mechanism between the guided wave and the bolted joint, which adversely impacts the accuracy of bolt preload detection. In this paper, we develop a two-dimensional frequency domain finite element model (FDFEM) for a bolted joint plate. We first analyze the excitation efficiency of each mode at varying excitation frequencies and identify the optimal excitation intensities for the A0 and S0 modes. Subsequently, we examine the influence of the contact length (L) on the energy transmission coefficients of each mode. The results reveal that mode transformation occurs following the interaction between the single mode guided wave and the bolt joint surface. Furthermore, the energy transfer coefficients of each mode guided wave exhibit periodic variations with respect to L. Under A0 excitation conditions, the energy transfer coefficient is more sensitive to changes in L, making it suitable for early detection of bolt loosening. Conversely, under S0 excitation conditions, the energy transfer coefficient exhibits changes with L over a longer duration, rendering it more appropriate for the comprehensive detection process of the bolt, from the tightened state to complete loosening.

articleTitle: The Nonlinear Formulation and Analysis of Frequency-Temperature Relations of Vibrations of Quartz Crystal Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study focuses on the nonlinear equations of quartz crystal plate in an incremental thermal field. The thermal elastic constants of quartz crystal material are from the analysis by Lee and Yong. With the believe that a nonlinear formulation might improve the frequency-temperature relation in the high-temperature region, the nonlinear strain and stresses are adopted for nonlinear equations of motion with the inclusion of the displacement gradient. The nonlinearity can also be expanded to the constitutive relations with higher-order elastic constants. Then the nonlinear vibration equations are solved for the harmonic solutions of deformation and consequently the vibration frequencies with the known temperature are obtained by the extended Galerkin method (EGM). From the systematic analysis with the considerations of temperature and amplitudes of the displacements, the frequency-temperature relations are calculated and compared with both analytical and experimental results. The results in the high-temperature region is improved slightly. This procedure demonstrates the necessity to consider the nonlinearity in the refined analysis of thermal effect and behavior of quartz crystal resonators.

articleTitle: Performance Measurement of Piezoelectric Transformer under Compressive Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric transformer (PT) is an electronic device made of the material of piezoelectric ceramic, and utilizes the positive inverse piezoelectric effects to carry out the energy conversion between the electrical energy and the mechanical energy twice, so as to realize the function of the voltage change. Compared with the traditional electromagnetic transformer, PT has many advantages such as high frequency response, high power density and excellent conversion efficiency. In order to improve the working reliability, generally the PT needs to work under a certain pre-tensioned compressive stress. Therefore, for better use of PTs, it is necessary to study the efficiency of piezoelectric transformers operating under different compressive stresses. In this paper, firstly, the PT were applied with compressive stress T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> parallel to the direction of polarization and compressive stress T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> perpendicular to the direction of polarization, with no compressive stress as the initial state, to study the change rule of the efficiency under different stress conditions through simulation analysis. The results show that the efficiency of PT increases and then decreases with the increase of compressive stress T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> parallel to the polarization direction, and decreases all the time with the increase of compressive stress T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> perpendicular to the polarization direction. Finally, in this paper, the efficiency test is carried out by building an experimental platform and applying the compressive stress T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> parallel to the polarization direction of the PT, and the experimental results are consistent with the simulation.

articleTitle: A Miniature Piezoelectric Motor Based on the Impact Inertia Driving Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A high-precision miniaturized inertial piezoelectric motor that can achieve precision drive positioning work in a limited space is presented in this study. The overall size of the motor is a flat rectangle of 10 mm × 10 mm × 1.6 mm, which consists of a stator made of spring steel, a piezoelectric stack, and a friction foot. The experimental results show that the sample motor achieves a maximum speed of 5.26 mm/s and a maximum vertical load capacity of 1.2 N with a driving voltage of 60 Vp-p and a frequency of 3kHz, while the minimum resolving power of the sample motor is 21 nm. This new type of motor can be widely used in a wide range of miniaturized precision instruments, such as cameras, micro-robots, etc., due to the advantages of a smaller size and a higher resolving power.

articleTitle: Application of Symmetrization of Coefficient Matrix in the Wave Equation for Acoustoelastic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper mainly discusses the application of coefficient matrix symmetrization in the acoustic-elastic coupled wave equation. By performing matrix symmetrization transformation on the acoustic wave equation and the elastic wave equation, it is transformed into a form suitable for stability proof by using the energy method, and the SMF system is established. Based on this, a universal discrete framework is constructed by combining the SBP-SAT method, and PML/MPML is introduced to improve the wave absorption effect at artificial boundaries. The energy method is transformed to the frequency domain to prove the stability of the discrete system. This method can realize the SBP-SAT simulation of elastic wave-acoustic wave coupling in the 2 D case, simplify the derivation of the acoustic wave equation and the program compilation process. The simulation results show that it can solve different types of wave problems at a lower computational cost, and this method is expected to be extended to other wave equations.

articleTitle: Directional Elastic Transmission of Phononic Crystals with Chiral Resonant Units
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Directional wave transmission from periodic structures is enormously attractive in many potential applications. In this work, we present various types of two-dimensional square chiral phononic crystals and research their directional transmissions of elastic waves, which is utilized by isofrequency curves. Numerical calculations of band structures and transmission vibration modes are performed utilizing the finite element method. The transmission mechanism is analyzed by the isofrequency curves. The numerically calculated results show the good transmission properties of elastic waves at broad angles of chiral structures.

articleTitle: A FPGA-Based Integrated System for Guided Waves Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Guided waves communication has great potential to replace standard communication technologies in next-generation structural health monitoring (SHM) systems due to its ability to penetrate enclosed metallic structures while avoiding the Faraday effect. This study presents a FPGA-based integrated system for guided waves communication. The system includes a high-frequency, high-voltage transmission module and a high-sampling-rate reception module, using FPGA as the processor to control high-frequency guided waves excitation and edge data demodulation, enabling long-distance, high-speed data transmission. Compared to experimental instruments, the designed communication system achieves over 90 % size reduction and error-free real-time transmission.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Analysis of Rigid-Flexible System for Three-Axis Stabilized Spacecraft Considering Electromechanical Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of flexible vibration of the rigid-flexible coupled model in the process of motion, the dynamic modeling and analysis of the rigid-flexible model considering the influence of electromechanical coupling are studied. Based on Lagrange's principle, the ordinary differential equations of motion and partial differential equations of flexible parts of a three-dimensional rigid-flexible model are deduced to realize the coupling dynamics calculation between the flexible parts and the rigid body. On this basis, the piezoelectricity intrinsic is introduced to establish the continuum kinetic equation of the rigid-flexible coupling considering the effect of electromechanical coupling. The accuracy and reliability of the derived model are verified by means of Comsol simulation in the time and frequency domains, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Piezoelectric Energy Harvester Based on Wave Energy Collecting
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Wave energy reserves are abundant in the marine environment, but the low-frequency motion form of waves results in their energy not being easily collected. Therefore, this paper proposes a swing-type piezoelectric wave energy harvester (SPWEH). The device utilizes an oscillating plate to collect the kinetic energy generated by wave oscillations and then increases the rotor rotation frequency through a gear transmission mechanism. The magnetic coupling excitation using multiple rotating magnets further increases the excitation frequency. The magnetic coupling model and the electromechanical coupling model of the device are established in the theoretical analysis. The modal parameters of the piezoelectric vibrator are determined in modal simulations. The magnetic and deformation simulation results show that the maximum deformation of the piezoelectric vibrator with the tuning magnet is 8.839 mm, which is a 48.6% increase in deformation compared to the case without the tuning magnet.

articleTitle: NBBT95/5 Single Crystal Based Radial Extension Mode Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer for Range Finding
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study investigates a high-performance piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) based on 0.95(Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>)TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-0.05BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(NBBT95/5) single crystal material that can be used for ultrasonic ranging. NBBT95/5 is a lead-free and environmentally friendly piezoelectric material with a d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</inf> as high as 450 pC/N, which is much higher than d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</inf> of aluminum nitride (AlN) with a value of about 5 pC/N. To verify the reliability of the design, we prepared a NBBT based plate piezoelectric vibrator, and the test results of the vibrator are basically consistent with the simulation results. Based on the verification of the simulation reliability, a high-performance low-frequency PMUT with a resonant frequency of 83.8 kHz is designed for the application of ultrasonic ranging. Based on the simulation, the device's performance is notably superior to AlN-based PMUTs, boasting an effective electromechanical coupling coefficient of 2.7%, a dynamic displacement sensitivity of 6.2 μm/V, and a detection range of 6.5 m.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Laser Ultrasonic Detection of Elliptic Internal Defects under Constrain Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the laser-generated longitudinal waves (L waves) under the surface constrain mechanism with glass coating were simulated to detect and evaluate the internal elliptic defects in aluminum blocks. A plane strain model based on discontinuous Galerkin finite element method (dG-FEM) was established to study the effect of glass thickness on L waves and their interaction with the internal elliptic defects. The simulation results showed the improved directivity and increased amplitude of L waves related to the thickness of glass coating, and that the arrival times of the reflected L waves depended on the positions and sizes of the ellipses. Based on the arrival times of these enhanced reflected L waves, a novel method was developed to evaluate the elliptic defects. The relative error of location evaluation was below 0.9 %, and the sizing error was below 2.6 % by selecting the suitable received signals.

articleTitle: A Design of Quartz Crystal Microbalance Immune Sensing System for Ovarian Cancer Tumor Markers Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: For solution phase immunosensing of quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) in clinical oncology, it is hard to implement quantitative molecular diagnosis. Generally, the QCM resonator is unstable in liquid phase sensing. Meanwhile, the immune-reaction sensitivity is limited by molecular mass transport and the concentration of antigen-antibody complexes is limited by the design of partial electrode sensing. In this study, a novel high speed continuous flow and whole electrode occupation quartz crystal immunosensor has been developed for detection the levels of HE4, CA125, CEA, AFP and CA19-9 in ovarian cancer. The performance of QCM solution phase sensing system such as stability and immunoassay analysis time were investigated, respectively. The resonant frequency was stable within 2 Hz and the analysis time was only 6 min. The detection range for HE4, CA125, CEA, AFP and CA19-9 obtained by the proposed QCM sensing system were 200-8000 pmol/ml, 13.95-200 U/ml, 10-160 ng/ml, 10.4-800 ng/ml and 14-200 kU/L, respectively. It demonstrated that the proposed QCM sensing system may be able to offer good detection performance on ovarian cancer tumor markers from clinical serum.

articleTitle: The Design of a Ring Underwater Acoustic Broadband Transducer
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a underwater acoustic transducer is designed suitable for medium and high frequency underwater acoustic communication network. The active element of the transducer is the piezoelectric ceramic circular tube. Using the coupling of radial vibration and bending vibration of the circular tube to widen the working band of the transducer, the air backing ring transducer namely ABRT is made. The radial vibration of the transducer and the resonance of the inner water cavity improved the low frequency response of the transducer. The overflow loop transducer, namely FFRT, was made. The performance of the two transducers is comparable. The two transducers are combined coaxically through the connecting rod to form a combined transducer. The transmission voltage response level and reception sensitivity response level of two transducers, AABRT and FFRT, are tested. We propose improvement ideas based on the measured data, with the aim of obtaining smaller response fluctuations. This provides a new idea and design method for the broadband work of the circular transducer.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Low Frequency Flexible Transducers with High Bandwidth and Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Expanding the imaging field of view of medical probes helps doctors conduct more comprehensive examinations due to the larger visualization range. This paper presents a flexible-rigid dual-backing process for optimizing the bandwidth and flexibility of a 3MHz low-frequency flexible variable curvature phased array (FCPA) on the abdomen. The results show that FCPA has a bandwidth of up to 67.7% and high flexibility, which can achieve dynamic adjustment of the imaging field of view within 120°. The axial and lateral resolutions of phased array (PA) 30° and field of view 120° are 0.35mm and 0.77mm, 0.36mm and 1.02mm at depth of 80mm respectively. The CNR is 1.622.

articleTitle: First-Principles Calculations of Flexoelectric Coefficients in Perovskite Oxide Superlattices
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Discovering dielectric materials with large flexoelectric coefficients is key to advancing electromechanical devices. Using first-principles calculations, we determine the longitudinal and transverse flexoelectric coefficients of perovskite superlattice materials composed of ATiO3 (A=Pb, Ba, Sr). Our results show that the longitudinal flexoelectric coefficients of these superlattices are approximately four times larger than those of their parent bulk materials, respectively. This enhancement in the flexoelectric effect is attributed to charge transfer and interfacial interactions, which strongly influences the polarization in perovskite superlattice systems. These results can provide a guidance for searching for composite materials with large flexoelectric coefficients.

articleTitle: Research on Ultrasonic Synthetic Aperture Defect Imaging and 3D Reconstruction Method for Metal Component Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Focusing Technology is widely used in the detection of internal defects in metal components within industries such as manufacturing. When combined with three-dimensional reconstruction technology, it can reveal internal structures. However, during ultrasonic wave propagation, phenomena such as attenuation may occur. On the other hand, the quality of imaging is limited by hardware costs and data processing methods. This paper presents a method for defect imaging and three-dimensional reconstruction based on ultrasonic SAFT. In the numerical simulation, a test block model was established with defects incorporated. A single transducer was used to excite and receive signals, and an adaptive time gain compensation curve was employed to optimize signal gain. By integrating the dynamic threshold with the Marching Cubes algorithm, three-dimensional reconstruction of the defects was achieved. The result of the numerical simulation demonstrates that the proposed method can quickly and accurately detect the internal structures of metal components.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of High Deformability Morphing Wing Driven by Multi-Layer Parallel MFC Bimorphs with Adjustable Axial Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: To further improve the actuation performance and reliability of the chordwise variable camber wing driven by MFC bimorphs, this study proposes a morphing wing scheme using compliant rolling joint (CRJ) parallel multilayer MFC bimorphs with axial pressure controlled by twisted and coiled polymer actuator (TCPA). In this study, based on the three-dimensional homogenization parameters of MFC materials and the equivalent mechanical model of TCPA, a finite element model of multi-layer parallel TCPA-MFC pre-compressed bimorph actuators (TM-PBA) chordwise variable camber wing is established. The finite element simulation results show that the inter-layer support and tensile stiffness of CRJ can reach more than 10 times of the inter-layer shear stiffness. Under the condition of applying controllable axial pressure from 0N/0N/0N to 30N/30N/34N and maximum driving voltage (1500V/-500V), the trailing edge free displacement of the morphing wing without skin can be increased from 13.1 mm to 25.6 mm, and the blocking force can be increased from 1.70 N to 2.40 N. For the morphing wing with skin, the free displacement of the trailing edge can be increased from 8.54 mm to 16.7 mm, and the blocking force can be increased from 1.63 N to 2.25 N.
