Compared with morphing wing driven by multi-layer MFC-PBAs, the free displacement of the TM-PBAs wing is increased by one times, the blocking force is increased by about 30 %, and the design space is more than doubled.

articleTitle: Sound Absorption by the Phononic Crystal with Periodic U Hard Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In recent years, increasing interest on broadband low-frequency underwater sound absorption by the phononic crystal has been aroused. Due to water’s much longer wavelength, underwater metamaterials reported mostly have weak working effects on broadband frequency band and high underwater acoustic absorption. Therefore, the phononic crystal comprising novel solid structure and soft cavity in this paper is proposed, focusing on underwater sound absorption in potential practical application. Through U inclusions embedded in acoustic rubber underwater, several resonator modes are stimulated portably, inducing that working absorption frequency range is broadened a lot. The numerical results reveal that the resonator mode is always accompanied with transformation of sound propagation in solid medium. In addition, amplitude of deformation for the phononic crystal could also stimulate the underwater sound absorption effectively.

articleTitle: A Planar Deepwater Transducer based on Relaxor Ferroelectric Single Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The performance improvement of underwater acoustic transducers is intrinsically related to the utilization of high performance active material. A planar deepwater transducer consisting of a relaxing ferroelectric single crystal with a rectangular single crystal element polarized along the [011]c direction is proposed. The design incorporates a concave curved housing to promote in-phase vibration, while using multiple identical small units to drive a large radiant panel.The expansion of the radiant panel not only reduces the operating frequency and synchronizes the phase of the multi-unit vibration, but also allows it to be directly exposed to the fluid environment, allowing it to effectively withstand hydrostatic pressure. This structure can isolate the internal space from the external fluid. Compared with PZT piezoelectric ceramics, the relaxor ferroelectric single crystal has superior piezoelectric coefficient, which enhances the transmitting response of transducer. In addition, unlike convex curved shells, concave shells can prestress piezoelectric elements, significantly increasing the transducer's resistance to hydrostatic pressure.

articleTitle: State Parameter Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery Based on Ultrasonic Transmission Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: State of Charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) are key indicators for evaluating the operating status of lithium-ion batteries. Accurate detection and estimation of these parameters are crucial for ensuring the safe operation of batteries, achieving high-performance charging and discharging, and extending battery life. In this work, a non-destructive testing platform based on ultrasonic transmission characterization is developed. It enables real-time collection of acoustic parameters during the cycling process of a commercial pouch battery. Initially, using a cycle rate of 1C, the battery underwent 30 full cycles to develop a comprehensive database of characteristic parameters for SOC estimation. Next, the impact of discharge rate on battery capacity decay is investigated. The experimental results demonstrate that increasing the discharge rate accelerates battery capacity decay. Based on these research results, the commercial pouch battery is cycled at a high discharge rate, and characteristic parameters are extracted in real time to establish a database for SOH estimation. Subsequently, these databases are used to achieve precise estimation of SOC and SOH by employing a relevance vector machine (RVM) model. This approach provides a new research path for the non-destructive quantification of lithium-ion battery state parameters.

articleTitle: Symmetrization of Coefficient Matrix for Two-Phase Media Wave Equation and its SBP-SAT Difference Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Symmetrization of the coefficient matrix of the wave equation is an effective method to integrate different types of wave equations and reduce the difficulty of wave propagation simulation. It has been successfully applied to acoustic wave equations and elastic wave equations in isotropic and anisotropic media. In this paper, the symmetric format of the coefficient matrix of the two-term medium wave equation will be derived. Subsequently, a multi-axis perfectly matched layer is introduced, and the upwind scheme SBP-SAT difference method is used to discretize the wave equation, and the stability is evaluated by the energy method. Numerical simulations show that the proposed discrete framework has the characteristics of high integration, good stability and strong expansibility. In addition, the method in this paper can stably simulate wave propagation in curved domains and reduce its implementation cost, indicating that the symmetrization method of the coefficient matrix of the wave equation and its discrete framework have broad application prospects in the field of wave propagation simulation.

articleTitle: Elastic Constants Inversion of Zirconium Tube Based on the Longitudinal Mode of Guided Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Estimating elastic constants in materials is markedly important in engineering and technology. Ultrasonic guided wave non-destructive testing provides an effective means for accurately assessing material properties. This paper presents a method for inverting the elastic constants of hollow pipes using the longitudinal mode of ultrasonic guided waves combined with a genetic algorithm (GA). The Legendre orthogonal polynomial expansion (LOPE) method serves as the forward model for analyzing the dispersion curves of axisymmetric guided wave modes, while the GA performs the inversion. A carefully designed finite element (FE) model generates pseudo-experimental data, which is transformed into the frequency-wave number domain for input into the GA. The comparison between simulation results and theoretical analysis confirms the validity of the FE model and the accuracy of the detected modes. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively inverts the elastic constants of isotropic hollow cylindrical structures, with an inversion error of less than 2% based on pseudo-experimental data.

articleTitle: Dispersion Characteristics of Lamb Waves in Piezoelectric Nanoplates with Surface Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Based on the surface effect theory, the dispersion characteristics of Lamb waves in piezoelectric nanoplates with surface effects are studied. The dispersion relation is obtained by the Legendre polynomial method, which can transform the wave control partial differential equation-solving problem into a matrix eigenvalue problem yielding the full spectrum. The influences of surface piezoelectric parameters and plate thickness on the dispersion of Lamb wave are illustrated. Results show that changes in surface elasticity, surface piezoelectricity, surface dielectric properties, and surface density all significantly affect the dispersion behavior of Lamb waves. The propagation of Lamb waves in nano piezoelectric plates exhibits significant size dependence. When the plate thickness is small, the influence of surface effects is particularly prominent. As the plate thickness gradually increases, the influence of surface effects gradually weakens until it can be ignored.

articleTitle: Method for Measuring the Tightening Status of Bolts based on Nonlinear Ultrasonic Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Accurate and non-destructive detection of bolt tightening status is essential for ensuring the stability and safety of connection structures. To address the challenges posed by existing detection methods, such as insensitivity and complexity during the early stages of bolt loosening, this paper employs vibration-acoustic modulation technology in nonlinear ultrasonics and establishes a dynamic response model of the bolt connection interface based on the 'opening and closing theory.', and derives the relationship between the amplitude of the nonlinear response side lobe and the torque applied to the bolt. Furthermore, an improved looseness index is introduced to characterize the tightening status of the bolt. The feasibility of the detection scheme was analyzed and verified using COMSOL software. Finally, a nonlinear ultrasonic bolt tightening status detection experimental system was established. Utilizing pre-calibrated parameters, the connection tightening status of 6.8-grade M8 bolts was assessed. The measurement error and repeatability error were found to be less than 1 N-M and 0.8 N<M, respectively, within the torque range of 3-18 N-M. The experimental results indicate that the nonlinear ultrasonic method for detecting bolt tightening status proposed in this article is indeed feasible.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of Nonlinear Interaction of Guided-Wave Mixing and Micro-Cracks in Pipes
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Pipes are widely used in various industries but are subject to plastic deformation and corrosion, during which microcracks may appear. Ultrasonic guided wave mixing has gained attention due to its high sensitivity. This study employs phase inversion and two-dimensional Fourier transform to investigate the nonlinear interaction between counter-propagating guided waves and microcracks. The generated sum-frequency components and difference-frequency components contain multiple flexural modes and propagate toward both ends of the pipeline. The generated sum-frequency components and difference-frequency components are used to locate the microcracks. The circumferential location of the microcracks is determined by polar diagrams (i.e., the amplitudes of difference-frequency or sum-frequency components and angles), while the axial location is determined by the relationship between the amplitudes of difference-frequency components or sum-frequency components and distance.

articleTitle: Defect Imaging Technique for Electrical Porcelain Bushings Utilizing Laser-Excited Thermal Diffusion Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper introduces a defect detection technique for electrical porcelain bushings utilizing laser-excited thermal diffusion waves. Electrical bushings, crucial in power transmission, are prone to defects due to various factors, posing significant threats. This technology applies controlled thermal excitation to specimens, manifesting internal defects as abnormal surface temperature distributions captured by infrared thermography. The effectiveness of the technique is investigated through ceramic bushing specimens with varying defect sizes and depths. Results demonstrate its capability to detect defects up to 12mm below the surface, with periodic excitation showing superior performance for deeper defects.

articleTitle: Scattering of Shear Horizontally Wave by An Elliptical Cavity in Exponentially Inhomogeneous Half Space
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: On the basis of complex function method, the SH save scattering problem by an elliptical cavity in an exponentially inhomogeneous half space is studied in this paper. The mass density of the half space is exponentially inhomogeneous while the shear modulus is a constant. With the help of a pair of complex transformation, the governing equation with variable coefficients is transformed into a standard Helmholtz equation. Using conformal mapping method, the elliptical cavity is mapped to be a unit circle. Then the boundary condition is constructed and the undetermined coefficients are solved. Finally, dynamic stress concentration factor (DSCF) at the cavity is calculated and discussed. Numerical results show that the value and the distribution of DSCF are influenced by the inhomogeneous parameter and the shape of the cavity evidently.

articleTitle: Design of Ultrasonic Generator Interface Communication and Enable Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper introduces two circuit designs for the interface of the ultrasonic generator. The original communication circuit is primarily designed based on RS485 communication principles, and it has issues with erroneous communication data due to excessive noise. We add isolation design and decoupling capacitors to reduce noise. The original enable circuit is primarily designed based on opto-isolation principles, and also experiences false triggering due to excessive noise. We incorporate a Schmitt trigger, RC low-pass filter and diode protection to stabilize the enable signal. Therefore, the communication signal can be transmitted stably to the ultrasonic generator for precise control.

articleTitle: Response of Functionally Gradient Material Under The Influence of SH Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: All In this paper, the wave propagation in functionally graded materials (FGM) is studied by the elastic wave theory based on the wave problems in homogeneous media. The auxiliary function and modulus function are introduced to construct the displacement field and density function. The displacement field, modulus function and density function are connected to propose a design theory of special functionally graded materials. An analytical method for elastic wave propagation in inhomogeneous media with varying modulus and density is derived to provide theoretical references for material design and dynamic stress analysis under elastic waves. Taking the problem of dynamic stress concentration caused by shallow buried elliptical cavity in half space designed under SH waves as an example, the calculation results are obtained and analyzed. The results show that the dynamic stress concentration (DSCF) is sensitive to the change of the inhomogeneity of the medium.

articleTitle: SH Wave Propagation Characteristics In Functionally Graded Viscoelastic Couple-Stress Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper studies the propagation characteristics of SH waves in functionally graded viscoelastic (FGVE) couple-stress plates. Based on the modified couple stress theory, the Legendre orthogonal polynomial method (LOPM) and Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic model were combined to solve the dispersion characteristics of SH waves in the FGVE couple-stress plates. The influences of the couple stress, viscoelasticity and inhomogeneity of medium on the dispersion relationship are discussed. It shows that the couple stress effect and inhomogeneity strengthen the attenuation of SH wave.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Studies on Detecting Wheelset Tread Defects by Surface Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Train wheels, as an important component of the train, it is inevitable to generate long-term complex friction with the railway track, which can lead to defects in the wheel tread. Owing to the influence of oil stains on the surface of the wheelset, existing methods may miss detection when detecting small defects. To address this problem, we proposed a detection method for wheel tread defects using surface waves. The interaction between surface waves and wheel tread defects was analyzed through simulation. The results indicated a positive correlation between the reflection coefficient and the defect depth and a negative correlation between the transmission coefficient and the defect depth. The reflection and transmission coefficients are more sensitive when the defect depth is in the first half wavelength range of the surface wave, which provides a basis for the parameter selection of surface waves. Finally, an experimental platform for detecting defects in the wheel tread has been established, and an experimental study on detecting cracks of different depths has been conducted. The results showed that the transmission coefficient can be used to detect the defect with a depth of 1 mm on the wheel tread and evaluate the defect depth. This study improves the accuracy of detecting defects on the wheel tread.

articleTitle: Fracture Behaviors of a Mode-I Crack in a Piezoelectric Semiconductor Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric semiconductors (PSCs) integrate piezoelectric effects with semiconductor properties, making them ideal for applications in acoustic wave devices, sensors, and energy systems. Despite their advantages, PSC ceramics often suffer from defects such as cracks and voids, highlighting the importance of studying their fracture behavior, especially under electromechanical coupling. This paper investigates the plane strain behavior of cracks in PSCs using Fourier transformation and singular integral equation techniques. Numerical results reveal that conductivity and applied loads significantly affect fracture behavior and provide the range of initial carrier concentrations influencing fracture parameters. These findings enhance the theoretical understanding and practical design of PSC devices, contributing to improved reliability and extended service life predictions.

articleTitle: Wind Tunnel Experimental Study on Hybrid Ice Protection Systems for Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Aircraft icing poses a significant threat to flight safety, making anti-icing technology a key focus in aerospace research. This paper investigates a novel hybrid anti-icing technology that combines electro-thermal and super hydrophobic coatings. Through experiments conducted in icing wind tunnel, the effectiveness of various anti-icing strategies was evaluated. The experimental results indicate that the electro-thermal and super hydrophobic coupled model not only effectively prevents ice formation but also reduces energy consumption. Furthermore, this system demonstrated no occurrence of runoff ice, exhibiting excellent anti-icing performance and economic viability. This study lays the groundwork for the future integration of piezoelectric excitation in anti-icing technology development.

articleTitle: Impact of Defect Alignment on Biaxial Stretching in Monolayer Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The primary objective of this study is to investigate the effects of defect regularity and randomness on the mechanical properties of monolayer graphene under biaxial tension through molecular dynamics simulations. Molecular dynamics was employed to analyze the failure processes of graphene films under various defect arrangements, yielding corresponding stress-strain relationships and fracture patterns. The results indicate that the presence of defects significantly reduces the mechanical properties and tensile strength of graphene. The impact of defect arrangement on mechanical properties varies. When the loading direction aligns with the defect distribution and has minimal effect on model stability, edge defects cause less structural damage compared to central defects. In contrast, when defect arrangement has a greater impact on structural stability, the structure is more prone to failure. Additionally, random defect distribution increases the average size of effective defects, thereby reducing fracture strength and adversely affecting the mechanical performance of graphene.

articleTitle: Enhanced coupling and sensitivity of Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers with electrode buried in Silicon dioxide
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this work, a high-sensitivity piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) with electrodes buried in silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) film is designed and fabricated. First, a PMUT on the proposed SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Pt/PZT/Pt/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si structure is modeled and simulated. The simulation results show that a larger effective electromechanical coupling coefficient $\left({k_{{\text{eff }}}^2}\right)$ of 2.24% and a higher transmitting sensitivity of 4.4 μm/V is simultaneously achieved. Then the proposed PMUT is fabricated, and the measured transmitting sensitivity compared well with the simulation one, which is 1.6 times larger than that of the conventional SOI-based PMUT. Besides, its resonant sound pressure level reached up to 94.5 dB. These investigation results demonstrated that the PMUT on the proposed structure offers enhanced coupling factor and transmitting sensitivity, which is beneficial for applications in long-distance ultrasonic detection. Additionally, this Si-based PMUT design enables a simple fabrication process and reduction of manufacturing cost for mass production.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lithium Niobate Xbar Resonator with Sandwich Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: With the large-scale application of 5G communication, the demand for high-frequency, large bandwidth and low insertion loss resonators are increasingly urgent. At present, the laterally-excited bulk acoustic resonator (XBAR) based on lithium niobate (LN) has the characteristics of high resonant frequency and high electromechanical coupling coefficient. However, due to the small thickness of LN film, stray modes are easily introduced, which seriously deteriorates the device performance. In this paper, an XBAR resonator based on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> substrate is designed, and the electrode is covered with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> temperature compensation layer. The device is simulated by COMSOL multi-physics coupling software, and the influence of several key parameters on the performance of the resonator is studied. The resonator uses A1 mode Lamb wave as the main mode, and through reasonable optimization of parameters, the simulation results show that the resonant frequency is 3.21GHz, the coupling number of electromechanical system can reach 45.7%, and quality factor (Q-factor) value at the resonance point is 1249. Compared with the traditional XBAR resonator, the electromechanical coupling coefficient is only reduced by 5%, and the quality factor is increased by 30%.

articleTitle: Wave Propagation in Piezoelectric Semiconductor Layered Nanoplates Based on Modified Couple Stress Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The time-harmonic wave propagation in three-dimensional (3D) piezoelectric semiconductor (PS) layered nanoplates is investigated with the modified couple-stress effect. According to the time-harmonic solutions of the extended displacement (i.e., mechanical displacements, electric potential, electron concentration perturbation), the elastic wave problem is converted into a linear eigenvalue system from which the extended displacements and stresses are expressed in terms of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. The dispersion equation is obtained by the boundary conditions and the propagator matrix method. Numerical examples are provided to show the influence of the initial carrier concentration, material length scale parameter, thickness of nanoplates and wavenumber on the dispersion curves in PS layered nanoplates.

articleTitle: Effect of Front Topography on Ground Motion of V-Shaped Canyons Under SH Waves Incidence
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this article, the theoretical model of seismic motion for the front canyon and hill topography rear V-shaped canyon is constructed based on the idea of Conjunction. The expression and derivation of the wavefield and shear stress in the partition model under horizontal SH wave incidences is provided. The theoretical solution of frequency-domain ground motion field in the front topography combination model is solved by combining boundary conditions. The accuracy and convergence of the solution is verified by the degradation and comparation with the classic cases. The influence of the type, distance, and size of the front topography on the ground field behind is mainly discussed. The numerical results show that the front topography will cause shielding effects on the seismic motion field behind, whether the front canyon or the hill. The shielding effect will be stronger as the distance decreases or the size increases, and the effect of the front canyon is slightly stronger than that of the front hill. This front topography shielding theory could be considered for application in the field of earthquake protection.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Micromechanical Ultrasonic Transducer Based on a “Double-Circle-Ear” Cavity Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a piezoelectric micromechanical ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) featuring a "double-circle-ear" cavity structure is proposed on the basis of a circle cavity structure to improve its acoustic performance. Based on the PZT piezoelectric thin film, a three-dimensional finite element simulation model is created for the PMUT cell using the finite element software COMSOL Multiphysics. This study investigated the resonance frequency, resonance displacement, and sound pressure level of the PMUT cell operating in (0,1) mode. The PMUT yields a resonance frequency of 64.27 kHz, a resonance displacement of 21,272 nm, and a sound pressure level at a distance of 10 cm from the upper surface of the center is 100 dB. Notably, the resonance displacement improves by 5303 nm, and the sound pressure level increases by 2 dB when compared to the traditional circle cavity design. The results indicate that the new PMUT with the "double-circle-ear" cavity structure emits stronger acoustic waves, allowing it to cover a larger range of distances for detection and imaging, which is beneficial to applications requiring long-distance detection.

articleTitle: Dynamic Stress Concentration of An Elliptical Cavity In Inhomogeneous Half Space Under SH-Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of dynamic stress concentration of an elliptical cavity in inhomogeneous half space under SH-wave is studied. Based on the theory of complex function method, the propagation characteristics of anti-plane shear waves in inhomogeneous half space are analyzed. Specific inhomogeneous parameters are introduced into the density function. Firstly, the conformal mapping method is employed to transform an elliptical cavity into a circular one, and a pair of complex variables are introduced to normalize the governing equation. Then, by utilizing the boundary conditions of the surface, the scattered waves, which conform to the stress-free conditions of the surface, are derived using the mirror image method. The undetermined coefficients in the scattering waves are then solved by applying the boundary condition at the elliptical cavity. Finally, the entire wave fields are numerically calculated, and the influence of various parameters on dynamic stress concentration is analyzed. The results indicate that the increase of dimensionless parameters kR and inhomogeneous parameters β will complicate the distribution of DSCF.

articleTitle: Impact Response of Sandwich Structure with Bidirectional Negative Poisson's Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In contemporary military and civilian infrastructure fields, many structures are subjected to the impact of explosive shock waves. Explosion shock waves have unique properties, including an initial increase in magnitude, rapid attenuation, and short duration. Therefore it is imperative to investigate the transient dynamic responses of these structures when subjected to such shock waves. The sandwich structure is extensively utilized in industries such as aerospace and transportation. Currently, researchers are actively exploring a myriad of structural design strategies aimed at augmenting the resilience of sandwich structures against explosive impacts. In this paper, a bidirectional negative Poisson ratio sandwich structure is proposed, which can significantly reduce the propagation of explosion shock wave compared with the traditional honeycomb sandwich panel. The explosion impact performance of the bidirectional negative Poisson’s ratio sandwich structure under different structural parameters is studied through numerical calculations, which provides some reference for the design of satellite structures in aerospace engineering.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Dispersion Effects on Ultrasonic Detection of Three-Dimensional Stress in Thick Steel Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of dispersion effects on a three-dimensional stress detection method for thick steel plates using transverse wave tri-refraction. It examines how phase velocities of quasi-shear and quasi-longitudinal waves vary with stress levels, plate thicknesses, and material properties. Experimental results show that phase velocity changes are relatively stable within the 0-5 MHz frequency range, while significant deviations occur above 5 MHz. The 2.5-5 MHz frequency range is identified as optimal due to its smoother dispersion curves, which enhance detection accuracy. The study also underscores the need to recalibrate specimens with varying thicknesses and materials to ensure precise stress detection.

articleTitle: Molecular Dynamics Investigation of Carbon Ion Irradiation for Defect Repair in Bilayer Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study investigates the mechanism of defect repair in bilayer graphene using carbon ion irradiation and its effects on mechanical properties. Molecular dynamics simulations were employed to systematically examine the interaction between carbon ions and defective graphene by controlling two key parameters: irradiation dose (15-90) and energy (1-10 eV).Our findings reveal that carbon ion irradiation enhances material performance through two mechanisms: strengthened interlayer interactions and localized defect repair. Under optimal conditions, the treated bilayer graphene exhibits significantly improved fracture strength. The repair efficiency strongly correlates with irradiation parameters, achieving optimal results within an energy range of 4-5 eV and a dose range of 40-70. However, excessive irradiation doses lead to new adsorption-type defects, while high energies cause structural damage.This work elucidates the fundamental principles of carbon ion irradiation for bilayer graphene repair. It presents a novel technical approach for developing efficient and controllable defect engineering in 2D materials, offering significant practical value for optimizing the performance and reliability of graphene-based electronic devices.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Vibration Isolation for Honeycomb Sandwich Plate by Locally Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The control and suppression of low frequency vibration and noise has always been a difficult problem in mechanical engineering. In the field of phononic crystals, the transmission of low frequency sound waves can be effectively controlled by local resonance. A honeycomb sandwich panel structure is established for the low frequency vibration disturbance. The dispersion curves, modal shape and transmission performance of the structure are analyzed, respectively. The influence of structural parameters on the characteristics of the energy band are further investigated. The regulation law of the bandgap is mastered. Phononic crystals have excellent vibration isolation performance within the bandgap. By adjusting the structural parameters of the locally resonance oscillator, the frequency of bandgap of vibration isolation has been tuned effectively. Excellent effect of vibration isolation has been achieved. A low frequency with 16~22 Hz has been obtained and low vibration transmission coefficient are achieved in a low frequency. The increase of the oscillator mass will shift the bandgap to lower frequency. At the same time, the increase in the thickness of the element will cause the bandgap to move to higher frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sweep Frequency Signal Based on Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study aims to explore the application of frequency sweep signal analysis based on discrete Fourier transform in complex environments, in order to improve the accuracy and reliability of signals. Firstly, the significance and application of discrete Fourier transform in signal processing are elucidated. Subsequently, the properties of frequency sweep signals and the challenges they bring in practical scenarios are introduced in detail. Given the complexity of frequency sweep signals, a method based on discrete Fourier transform is proposed. By converting the signal to the frequency domain for spectral analysis, this method can identify the frequency components and energy distribution in the swept frequency signal, thereby promoting accurate analysis and processing of the swept frequency signal. The experimental results show that the use of discrete Fourier transform for frequency sweep signal analysis can effectively extract signal features, reduce noise signal interference, and provide strong support for signal processing and recognition. Therefore, this method has great application prospects in various fields such as communication, radar, and medicine.

articleTitle: Exact Solution for Scattering of SH-Waves by a Locally Asymmetric Bump in an Elastic Half-Space
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Geometric features, particularly bump, on elastic media surfaces greatly impact wave propagation, affecting material mechanical properties and structural response. In this study, a novel analytical method is proposed to solve the interaction between trapezoidal and triangular surface bump of a half-space medium and SH waves using the wave function expansion and complex variable methods. This approach is applicable to both the symmetric and asymmetric cases. First, based on the multipole partition technique, two semicircular auxiliary boundaries were introduced to divide the model into three simpler enclosed regions. Second, a new approach for constructing displacement functions is proposed, which allows the translation of polar coordinates in both the vertical and horizontal directions while ensuring the convergence of the solution. Finally, the differences brought about by the asymmetric assumptions in the trapezoidal and triangular protrusion problems under various incident angles are analyzed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wave Propagation in Flexoelectric Beam Using Mixed Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A dynamic model of flexoelectric Timoshenko beams is established to investigate wave propagation characteristics. The dispersion curves of bending and shear waves are numerically obtained using the mixed finite element method (FEM). Compared with pure elastic beams, the flexoelectric effect increases the effective stiffness of the beam, leading to higher frequencies of bending and shear waves. This frequency increase becomes more pronounced at higher wavenumbers. Additionally, the study reveals a significant size-dependent characteristic of the flexoelectric effect, which is more pronounced at the nanoscale and diminishes with increasing beam thickness.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Characteristics of V-Shaped Ultrasonic Motor Based on Nonlinear Current Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In the actual operation of ultrasonic motors, their real-time output speed and thrust are closely related to the real-time input voltage and current. Judging the output mechanical characteristics by the input electrical characteristics can greatly simplify the fault diagnosis of the motor. Therefore, it is very necessary to establish a corresponding model to study the change law of the electrical characteristics of ultrasonic motors. This paper establishes a current prediction model based on the dynamic model and equivalent circuit model of the V-shaped ultrasonic motor (VSUM). The model takes into account the nonlinear effect brought by the change of preload. Through this model, the electrical characteristics of the ultrasonic motor under different working conditions can be predicted. Finally, the accuracy of the current prediction model is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Directional Piezoelectric Excitation Platform: Design, Analysis and Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In various fields, including mechanical engineering and aerospace, vibration excitation platforms play a crucial role in quality inspection and reliability assessments. As the demand for multidirectional capabilities, integration, and high precision increases, the development of a novel piezoelectric excitation platform has become imperative. A multi-directional piezoelectric excitation platform is designed, analyzed and experimented. First, the proposed platform is designed to consist of four piezoelectric actuators and is equipped with flexure Hook joints. In addition, the proposed platform can excite longitudinal vibration and multi-directional bending vibration, and the operating principle is analyzed by the finite element method. Finally, a prototype was fabricated and the measurement system was constructed. The experimental results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed platform, achieving vibration excitation with a maximum acceleration of 4.17 m/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This lightweight and compact piezoelectric vibration excitation platform shows great potential for inducing longitudinal and multi-directional bending vibrations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Internal Stress on the Resonant Frequency of Bender Disks
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Bender disk is a typical low-frequency transducer structure, primarily utilizing its bending vibration modes for the conversion between mechanical and electrical energy. The article investigates the control of residual stress levels by adjusting the interference fit in a bending vibrating disk structure. It also conducts modal simulations and experimental measurements of resonant frequencies under the influence of contact stresses acting on the structure. Both simulation and experimental results indicate that the magnitude of residual stresses has an effect on the resonant frequencies of the bender vibrating disk; bigger residual stresses lead to higher resonant frequencies of the structure. Furthermore, the experimental measurement results show that with the interference fit of the test samples ranging from 0.005 mm to 0.11 mm, the maximum variation amplitude of the resonant frequency is around 5%. However, once the interference fit reaches a certain value, the resonant frequency remains virtually unchanged. The article uses interference fit to establish the relationship between curved discs and internal stress, and innovatively uses numerical simulation and experiments to obtain the relationship between internal stress and its resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Research on High-Efficiency Enrichmen Technology of Metal Wear Particles in Lubricating oil Based on Acoustic Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: By analyzing wear particles in the lubrication system, it is possible to gain insights into the wear characteristics and mechanisms of mechanical components. Although various detection and analysis methods exist, the pretreatment for enriching these tiny debris remains complex and time-consuming. Traditional physical filtration and magnetic attachment techniques have limitations in terms of efficiency and selectivity. This paper presents an acoustic manipulation chip (AMC) platform that utilizes combined acoustic forces to achieve efficient enrichment of both magnetic and non-magnetic metal particles from lubricating oil samples. By adjusting the excitation frequency and voltage, the platform generates specific acoustic field within microchannels, driving particles to move toward the central region for enrichment. This innovative approach provides a new perspective for developing filter-free automatic preprocessing tools.

articleTitle: Influence Of The Thickness Of The Adhesion Layer On The Contact Surface On The Output Performance Of A V-Shaped Ultrasonic Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Frictional wear at the stator/rotor contact interface can lead to changes in friction characteristics and instability in motor operation, limiting their application. This study focuses on the frictional properties of the stator/rotor contact, exploring the mechanism of adhesive layer formation and its impact on motor operating characteristics. Firstly, the operating mechanism of the motor and the formation mechanism of the adhesive layer are analyzed. Subsequently, based on mixed lubrication tribology theory, a friction coefficient estimation model is established, and the influence of adhesive layer thickness on the friction coefficient is investigated. Simultaneously, a dynamic model of the linear ultrasonic motor is constructed to analyze the impact of the friction coefficient on motor operating characteristics. Finally, methods for measuring the thickness of the adhesive layer are proposed, and experimental studies on the variation of adhesive layer thickness over time and its impact on the friction coefficient and motor operating characteristics are conducted. Experimental results show that the thickness of the adhesive layer increases over time, while the friction coefficient, operating speed, and thrust initially decrease and then increase.

articleTitle: Modeling and Experimental Investigation of Array Multisource Energy Harvester in Series
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: With the aim of expanding the illumination area and broadening the resonant frequency range, an array multisource energy harvester connected in series was proposed. The mathematical model of the array multisource energy harvester taking into account the anomalous photovoltaic and piezoelectric effects was derived. Numerical simulations and experimental verifications were carried out. The results demonstrate that the mathematical model is rational. The experimental findings show that under light with an intensity of 3 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and vibration of 1 g@28 Hz, the maximum output power of three harvesters connected in series reached 707 μW, which is three times as high as the output of a single cantilever beam.

articleTitle: A High-Resolution Non-Destructive Evaluation Method for Aircraft Rivets Using the Ultrasonic Array
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Rivet cracks, resulting from stress concentration around the fastener hole, are the main sources of failure in aircraft structures. Traditionally, the inspection includes visual detection off-line and single ultrasonic probe detection around the rivet surface. However, the visual method needs to break the rivet structures and can’t achieve non-destructive detection. Single ultrasonic probe detection is time-consuming and difficult to size cracks. To overcome the above limitations, we propose a novel detection method using ultrasonic arrays to realize a whole and accurate characterization of rivets. The full matrix capture (FMC) data is collected and the high-resolution image is produced by the total focusing method (TFM). We demonstrate the method by simulation and experiment. The result shows that our method could image the crack above 1 mm, and the measurement error is less than 5%. It verifies great potential in the high-resolution detection of aircraft rivet cracks.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Measurement of Contact Pressure of Bolted Joint Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Bolt joint connection is one of the most widely used connection method in the entire industrial technology field. The pressure distribution of the bolted joint interface, directly affect the performances of the bolted connection structure such as stiffness and sealing. Therefore, non-destructive measurement of the contact pressure on the bolted interface is of great significance. Ultrasonic methods can achieve non-destructive testing of the contact pressure of the jointed interface. However, this method relies on the experimental calibration of the ultrasonic reflection coefficient and contact pressure. How to optimize the calibration method has become a key issue affecting the detection of contact pressure. In this paper, an uncalibrated contact pressure measurement method based on ultrasound for bolted interface is developed. The contact pressure obtained by different calibration methods is compared. According to the comparison results, the calibration method of ultrasonic contact pressure measurement of bolted connection interface is optimized, so as to improve the detection accuracy of contact pressure. The experimental results show that the reflection coefficient-contact pressure curve constructed by calibration experiment can obtain more accurate contact pressure.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a High-Performance Circular PMUT with a Neck Cavity Based on ALN Film
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents a circular piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) based on aluminum nitride (AlN) film with a neck cavity. The structure is designed and optimized by the three-dimensional finite element method (3D-FEM). The influence of geometric parameters such as the Si layer thickness, radius of top electrode, and the radius of the neck cavity on the frequency, sensitivity and ${\text{k}}_{{\text{eff}}}^2$ is systematically studied to achieve a high-performance PMUT based on AlN film. The simulation results indicate that the optimal values for the Si layer thickness, top electrode radius, and neck cavity radius for the proposed PMUT are 2 μm, 130 μm, and 40 μm, respectively. The transmitting sensitivity is 149.65 nm/V and the receiving sensitivity is 4.352 V/kPa, representing increases of 1.32 times and 3.86 times compared to the traditional PMUT without the neck cavity, respectively. Furthermore, the ${\text{k}}_{{\text{eff}}}^2$ of the proposed PMUT reaches up to 1.45%, a significant 111.54% improvement over the traditional PMUT.

articleTitle: Element-Free Analysis of Functionally Graded Piezoelectric Inkjet Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: To improve the performance of piezoelectric inkjet actuators, a functionally graded piezoelectric inkjet actuator is proposed. Compared with the finite element method, the element-free method has significant advantages in solving heterogeneous and multi-field coupling problems. An element-free simulation model for the functionally graded piezoelectric inkjet actuator is established based on the first-order shear deformation theory. The influence of gradient factor, piezoelectric film thickness, and electric load on the performance of the functionally graded piezoelectric inkjet actuator is analyzed. The results indicate that the current results are in good agreement with the finite element results, which proves the accuracy of the element-free model. The performance of the functionally graded piezoelectric inkjet actuator is positively correlated with the gradient factor, piezoelectric film thickness and electric load. As the gradient factor increases from 0 to 3, the deformation of the functionally graded piezoelectric inkjet actuator increases by 29%. The performance of the functionally graded piezoelectric inkjet actuator is superior to the existing inkjet actuators based on piezoelectric ceramics and piezoelectric polymers.

articleTitle: Plane Stress Field Measurement of Steel Members in Service Based on Acoustic Path Difference Method
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Under complicated loads, the plane stress fields of steel members are unevenly distributed. The existing ultrasonic methods are limited by the size of the sensor, resulting in insufficient spatial resolution and failure to reveal the plane stress field of steel members. In this study, the acoustic path difference method is proposed to improve the spatial resolution of the plane stress field measurement. The innovation of this method is to decrease the acoustic path by calculating the acoustic time difference between two sets of acoustic paths. The measurement equation for the plane stress field is derived and the measurement system is designed. The signal processing system based on an interpolation algorithm and cross-correlation algorithm is established to capture the variations of acoustic time. The plane stress field of the H-beam is measured to verify the proposed method. The average deviations of measurement stresses between the proposed and strain gauges are less than 10 MPa, demonstrating the proposed method has high accuracy.

articleTitle: Fracture Damage Evolution of Piezoelectric Solids by Phase-Field Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Phase-field modeling (PFM) has been widely used in the field of pure mechanics, but the application in multi-physics coupling fields remains limited due to the complexity of fracture processes in these environments. To address the challenges of fracture in multi-material layered piezoelectric solids within an electromechanical coupling context, this paper employs a phase-field cohesive zone model (PF-CZM) specifically tailored for linear piezoelectric solids. The study investigates fracture evolution in piezoelectric bonded plates subjected to various electric field intensities. Numerical simulations of several representative cases are conducted to verify the accuracy of the electromechanical coupling phase-field model. Additionally, the impact of parameters, such as material properties and interface behavior, on crack evolution is systematically examined.

articleTitle: The Scattering Analysis of Guided SH-Waves in a Curved Plate
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) finite element method (FEM), for analyzing the scattering phenomenon of guided SH waves travelling through a curved plate with/without internal defects. By introduction of guided wave mode orthogonality, the displacement and traction fields of the scattered wave on a far-field cross section are expressed as the superposition of a series of propagating guided SH modes with reflection/transmission coefficients to be solved. Consequently, we establish the DtN boundary conditions by introduction of displacement and stress wave structures of each mode. As the application of the method, we calculate the reflected and transmitted wave fields by defects in a curved plate of different locations, and perform parametric analysis. The tendency of reflection coefficients with respect to defects’ parameters suggests the potential for quantitative non-destructive evaluation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of Crack Extension in Cf/ZrB2-SiC Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper proposes a crack extension prediction model that includes predicting the shape and length of cracks, based on a variety of deep learning technologies and optimization methods, using a large amount of data obtained from traditional numerical simulation experiments in the early stage. The model is implemented by first qualitatively predicting the distribution and damage morphology of cracks from a macroscopic perspective through a generative adversarial network, then quantitatively analyzing the specific dimensions of crack extension from a microscopic level through an artificial neural network, and finally comparing the predicted results with the simulation experiment results to further verify the effectiveness of the above methods. A finite element model is established for the microstructural sample plate of ultra-high temperature ceramic composite materials. A data sample set for crack extension prediction is constructed. A crack morphology extension prediction model is built by using an improved generative adversarial network to predict the distribution of cracks. The model's ability to learn important features is enhanced by adding an attention mechanism module to the traditional CDCGAN, thereby improving the quality of the generated crack morphology images.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning for Evaluating Internal Defect Sizes in Insulating Materials Using Simulated Ultrasonic Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Data-driven deep learning methods are widely used in ultrasonic testing for internal defects in electrical insulation components, but their effectiveness is constrained by the scarcity of real detection signals. Many studies focus on using the finite element method to generate lots of ultrasonic signals with diverse defect types. However, the differences between simulation and real detection signals limit the performance of machine learning. In view of this, a transfer learning-based internal defect sizes evaluation strategy is proposed in this paper. FEM simulations were performed to generate void defect ultrasonic detection signals for 45 uniformly distributed diameters from 0.4 to 2.6 mm, while 5 actual void defects within the same diameter range were fabricated to obtain experimental signals. A pre-trained CNN model was initially trained on simulation data, and then the fine-tuning method was applied using experimental data, ultimately achieving a void size evaluation error of less than 6%.

articleTitle: AC Electric Field Stability Of [110]-Poled Relaxor Ferroelectric Single Crystals For Power Ultrasonic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Power ultrasound is an eco-friendly technology widely used in industrial processing and medical therapy. The increasing demand for sustainable technologies has driven research into advanced materials to improve ultrasonic device performance. Relaxor ferroelectric (RF) single crystals are promising due to their excellent electromechanical properties, but the depolarization, which degrades the properties of RF crystals and shortens device lifespan, is a significant limitation. This study investigates the depolarization characteristics of [110]-poled PMN-0.26PT, Mn-doped PMN-0.30PT, and 0.3PIN-0.4PMN-0.3PT crystals under large AC fields. The results have shown depolarization occurring in PMNT, Mn-PMNT, and PIMNT under threshold fields of 0.56, 0.7, and 0.65 times their respective coercive fields E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. The loss tan δ and dielectric constant ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> were gradually increased and piezoelectric coefficient d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</inf> of Mn-PMNT and PIMNT reached ~1200 pm/V under the large AC field below threshold field. This study highlights the importance of enhancing the stability for RF crystals in power ultrasonic devices.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Piezoelectric Atomizing Nozzle for Photoresist Coating
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a piezoelectric atomizing nozzle applied to photoresist coating is designed. The structure of its vibration system is designed according to the application scenario. The liquid supply channel is designed in the central axis of the vibration system, and the front cover plate of the piezoelectric transducer and the amplitude transformer are integrated. The modal simulation analysis is carried out by COMSOL to verify the rationality of the design of the vibration system of the piezoelectric atomizer. The photoresist was atomized by a designed piezoelectric atomizer nozzle, and the particle size of atomized droplets was measured and analyzed. It was found that the atomized droplets had uniform distribution and small particle size, which was conducive to improving the coating quality of photoresist.

articleTitle: Single-Phase-Drive Standing-Wave-Type Rotation Ultrasonic Motors Using Piezoelectric Ceramic Hollow Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric ceramic hollow cylinders can be utilized to fabricate high-resolution rotation ultrasonic motor. 2 types of standing-wave motor based on coupled tangential-axial (TA) mode and longitudinal L-mode have been studied by using finite element method. The simulated results show that hybrid-mode motor (using both TA3 and L1 modes) has a greater mechanical output than that of single-mode motor (using only TA3 mode). A prototype motor of TA3-L1 hybrid modes has been fabricated using a piezoelectric cylinder with dimensions 20 mm OD, 16 mm ID, and 8 mm length. The measured resonance frequencies are close to simulated results. When driven by single-phase 206 kHz 60 Vpp continuous voltage, the motor has no-load speed of ~ 400 rpm, and stall torque of ~ 0.016 Nm. When driven by pulsed voltage, the motor exhibits a minimum step angle of ~ 20 μrad.

articleTitle: A P (VDF-TrFE) Planar Hydrophone
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper primarily presents the design of a planar hydrophone composed of the copolymer piezoelectric material P (VDF-TrFE). The simulation analysis of the hydrophone structure reveals the impact of varying size parameters on the hydrophone's response characteristics, and the optimal design of hydrophone size parameters is established. Based on the finite element analysis, the planar hydrophone prototype is developed and the performance test is conducted. The test results demonstrate that the hydrophone exhibits favourable frequency response characteristics and high sensitivity within the designated frequency band, thereby substantiating the viability of the proposed

articleTitle: Numerical Study of Nonlinear Rayleigh wave detection Of Closed Cracks
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The detection of closed cracks on structural surfaces is investigated using nonlinear Rayleigh waves through finite element numerical simulation. The location of closed cracks was achieved using single-point excitation and multi-point reception. A relationship was established between the acoustic nonlinearity parameter, crack length, and crack depth. The results indicate that although the acoustic nonlinearity parameter of the transmitted wave varies at different receiver position, its trend with crack size remains generally consistent. This method can detect cracks as small as 0.7 times the wavelength of the second harmonic. However, when the crack depth exceeds the detection wavelength, further depth assessment becomes challenging. This study provides a reference for detecting surface closed cracks.

articleTitle: Research on ultrasonic guided wave characteristics and defect detection of bolt based on Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic model
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Bolt support technology is widely used in underground and construction engineering fields fields due to its advantages of high adaptability, simple construction, and low cost. As a concealed project, bolt support requires regular testing of the anchoring quality to ensure its stability and prevent unnecessary safety accidents. As an important non-destructive testing method, ultrasonic guided wave method is widely used in the quality inspection of bolt anchoring due to its advantages such as long propagation distance, low attenuation, and wide acoustic field coverage. Therefore, it is necessary to have a profound understanding of guided wave characteristics and the defect types that may exist in bolt support. Based on this, this paper proposes a recursive Legendre polynomial series method (RLPSM) based on the Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic theory to study guided wave characteristics in cement grouted bolts. The relationship between guided wave velocity and attenuation in cement grouted bolts are revealed. Meanwhile, an experimental detection platform for cement grouted bolts is established, and the reliability of theoretical results is verified through experiments. The influences of different defect depths on guided wave characteristics are analyzed.

articleTitle: Pipeline Defect Detection Technology Based on Circumferential Horizontal Shear Guided Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the dispersion curve of circumferential horizontal shear (CSH) guided wave in pipeline is obtained based on finite element method, and CSH0 mode guided wave is selected for defect detection. In order to excite CSH0 mode guided wave successfully, a ring piezoelectric array transducer is designed in this paper. The simulation results show that this transducer can effectively excite CSH0 mode guided wave and realize defect detection.

articleTitle: Dispersion Analysis of Guided Waves Propagation in Cylindrical Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper analyses the dispersion characteristics of guided waves in cylindrical waveguides. Cylindrical waveguides are structures like pipes and rods, that allow propagation of waves along the longitudinal direction of the cylindrical structures. The governing equations of cylinder waveguides are introduced and mathematical derivations for wave propagation equations are stated in this paper in order to implement the algorithms for solving the dispersion equations of cylindrical guided waves. Two numerical examples for a solid rod and a hollow pipe, respectively, are illustrated to validate the studied method. The properties of the cylindrical guided waves are analysed and discussed. Results obtained from this study will not only provide extra insight on this study field but also highlight the extent at which cylindrical waveguides can be used in various industries like NDT, SHM and more.

articleTitle: Key Technologies for Improving the Imaging Quality of Concrete Inspection Based on Total Focusing
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Concrete, is prone to strong structural noise during ultrasonic inspection, which reduces the SNR and is detrimental to the inspection and determination of damages. A concrete ultrasonic array inspection method was proposed here. Firstly, the actual detection signal is digitally compensated and filtered to remove the probe ringing effect and recover the defect reflection echo; Then, by using TR processing to enhance the defect echo, the signal-to-noise ratio at the defect site was increased by approximately 7.6 dB; Next, the PCI algorithm will be used to correct the defect echo phase, further improving the signal-to-noise ratio by about 8.1 dB; Finally, high-resolution imaging of concrete structures is achieved through TMF.

articleTitle: Optimization for Hybrid Thermoelectric-Piezoelectric Energy Harvester Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A hybrid energy harvester incorporating thermoelectric (TE) and piezoelectric (PE) generators is capable of converting both waste heat and mechanical energy into electrical energy concurrently. In order to achieve higher output power, segmented TE materials are selected in TE part. The development of thermal-electrical-mechanical coupling model is indispensable for accurately predicting and optimizing its operational performance. In hybrid TE-PE energy harvester, the heat sink beam of the TE part also serves as the substrate layer for the PE part. Distribution of TE part thermoelectric field is obtained which affects length of heat sink beam and influences the vibration behavior of PE part. Therefore, there is thermal-electrical-mechanical coupling behavior in hybrid energy harvester. The governing equation for the nonlinear vibration of the PE part is established on the basis of Hamilton's principle. The output power of hybrid system is analyzed and thermal-electrical-mechanical model is developed. Numerical results show that material parameters and structure dimensions can concurrently influence the performance of both the TE and PE parts in the hybrid energy harvester. In order to have higher computational efficiency, a neural network is trained, and the data are collected from the calculation based on coupled model. The optimal material parameters for hybrid energy harvester with high output power of TE part and PE part concurrently are studied. Optimization method with combining neural network and thermal-electrical-mechanical coupled model will provide guidance for optimal design of hybrid TE-PE energy harvester.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Piezoelectric Monitoring Technology in Backfilling Mining Process
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In backfilling mining, controlling the backfilling roof is essential for managing surface subsidence. Currently, the collaborative roof control theory involving coal pillars, hydraulic supports, and backfilling materials is a key method for analyzing roof deformation. However, its reliance on simplified mechanical models for theoretical calculations of backfilling roof deformation has limited its effectiveness in addressing roof deformation under complex mining environmental conditions. To accurately assess the deformation of the roof under complex mining conditions, we propose a method for real-time monitoring of dynamic roof deformation during the backfilling mining process. This method utilizes piezoelectric material sensors, which provide crucial data to support the analysis of roof deformation in the context of a collaborative roof control mechanics model. Additionally, by analyzing the deformation of the roof, we can further evaluate the effectiveness of the backfilling process.

articleTitle: Mechanical Design and Motion Study of a Magnetically Controlled Bionic Crawling Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: As a new type of robot made of flexible materials, soft robots have significant potential for applications in biomedicine, space exploration and search and rescue due to their excellent flexibility, adaptability and suppleness. However, the currently published magnetically controlled soft robots generally have simpler structures and shorter motion steps. Therefore, the aim of this work is to optimize the gait of magnetically controlled soft robots and increase their motion step. We designed a magnetic field-driven inchworm-like soft robot and established the corresponding dynamics model. The effects of different structural size parameters on the robot's motion step were investigated and optimized using genetic algorithms. Through finite element simulation and experimental study, we compared the optimized solution and verified the significant improvement of the improved magnetically controlled soft body robot in terms of motion rate and structural stability, which provides a basis for further optimization in the future.

articleTitle: High-Performance Piezoelectric Ceramic Drive Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: An improved error-amplification-based driving power supply is proposed to achieve high-precision displacement control of piezoelectric ceramics. The design incorporates a voltage negative feedback error-amplification structure, utilizing a single-ended flyback converter and a Cockcroft-Walton voltage multiplier to generate a high-voltage DC output. Phase stability is enhanced through zero-point compensation and noise gain compensation strategies. Simulations and experiments conducted using Multisim and LTspice demonstrate that the power supply supports multi-channel synchronous output, drives load capacitances exceeding 250 nF, and delivers a 0-120 V output with a resolution below 8 mV, noise levels under 5 mV, and a data update cycle of less than 40 μs. The improved power supply meets the requirements for high-precision micro/nano-positioning applications.

articleTitle: Actuation Equations and Dimensionless Analysis of Piezoelectric Actuators Under Strong Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The application of piezoelectric actuators in structural vibration control has become quite mature, but it still faces the challenge of high voltage loading requirements. For membrane structures, the actuation force of the piezoelectric actuator must not only consider the generated bending moment but also take into account the effect of axial force. To address this, we adopt the nonlinear constitutive equations of electromechanical materials and derive the actuation equation of the actuator. To verify its effectiveness, the derived actuation axial force and bending moment are compared through simulations in COMSOL software. Furthermore, the actuation equation has been simplified through the analysis of Poisson’s ratio effect. A dimensionless analysis is then performed to propose optimization strategies for the actuation equations.

articleTitle: Research on Wing Skin Damage Detection and Positioning Method Based on Ultrasonic Lamb Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The wing bears the load task of the aircraft in flight. Due to the wide contact area between the wing and the external environment, the wing surface is prone to structural damage such as crack, corrosion and impact under long-term service. Therefore, timely detection of wing skin damage is very important to ensure flight safety. Based on the piezoelectric ultrasonic nondestructive testing technology, this paper collects the ultrasonic Lamb wave signals of each path in the detection area by deploying the piezoelectric sensor network, denoises the echo signal based on VMD algorithm, and improves the linear weight in path fusion to exponential weight, which has better convergence effect. An experimental platform was built to detect and locate the non penetrating damage with a length of 2mm, a width of 10mm, a length of 1mm and a depth of 4mm. The feasibility of the scheme and algorithm was verified.

articleTitle: Primary Resonance Characteristics Of PET Membranes Based On Coupling Of Temperature And Elastic Modulus Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Considering the influence in heat environment on the stability of polyethylene terephthalate film (PET film) during the transport process, a temperature related elastic modulus model for PET film was established by constant stretching experiments on the elastic modulus values of PET film at different hot air temperatures and fitting the data. The nonlinear vibration partial differential equation of printed PET film under uniform hot air temperature field is firstly established, and the amplitude-frequency response relation equation of the system is obtained by the application of multiscale method. The main parameter resonance characteristics of the printed PET film under the influence of parameters such as the amplitude of the external excitation force of the hot air and the temperature of the drying heat air were analyzed by MATLAB numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Far-Focused Pixel-Based Imaging Algorithm for Multi-Layered Media Defect Defection and its GPU Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: When applied to multilayer media inspection, ultrasonic phased array technology often faces challenges with low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in echo signals. In this study, an improved far-focused pixel-based (FPB) imaging method for detecting defects in multilayer media is proposed. First, the shortest path searching method is used to correct the time delay calculation. Second, the base-band delay multiply and sum (BB-DMAS) beamforming is utilized to replace traditional delay and sum (DAS) beamforming to fully exploit the spatial coherence of the captured data in the receiving and transmitting apertures, thereby effectively suppressing the noise and clutter in the signal. Finally, the proposed algorithm is implemented on graphics processing unit (GPU) to improve imaging efficiency. The experimental results show that the proposed method improves the average SNR by 55.0% and reduces the average resolution by 28.2% compared to DAS-FPB, while achieving a GPU-based acceleration ratio exceeding 100 times that of CPU computation.

articleTitle: Aircraft Skin Structure Vibration Suppression Based on Piezoelectric-Abh Hybrid Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The thin-walled structure of aircraft is susceptible to vibrations caused by aerodynamic loads, which can impact the performance and longevity of the electronic equipment integrated with it. To effectively reduce this wideband structural vibration, a novel hybrid vibration suppression approach is proposed in this paper. This approach combines a piezoelectric active control technique with a passive control technique using ABH (Acoustic Black Hole) effect. Both the ABHs and the piezoelectric elements were specifically designed for a simplified thin-walled structure, which serves as the skin for the electronic equipment. The study focuses on vibration responses in the frequency range of 5 to 2000 Hz, analyzing the effects of the proposed hybrid vibration control method. Simulation results indicate that the piezoelectric active control technique effectively mitigates the mode vibration response of the main skin structure. Additionally, the ABH, combined with damping materials, passively suppresses vibrations in the middle to high frequency range. The theoretical basis for the starting operation frequency due to the ABH effect is also discussed. This hybrid control system is designed to be easily implemented in engineering applications due to its straightforward control algorithm.

articleTitle: Integrated Design and Development of Ultrasonic Guided wave Chaos Detection System for Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Chaotic oscillator system is one of the effective methods for detecting weak signals. The technique of detecting weak signals in chaotic oscillator system is to use the sensitivity of non-equilibrium phase transition of chaotic oscillator to the system parameters and the immunity to noise signals to achieve the detection of weak signals in strong noise background. The different effects of the periodic signal and noise signal on the phase track diagram of the Dufrene system can be used to clearly discriminate whether the detected signal is mixed with a guided wave signal of the same frequency as the system, and thus identify defects.
