In the realization of the traditional ultrasonic wave-guide detection equipment, expand the functions of the instrument detection system and reduce its operational difficulties. LabVIEW is used as a platform to write software, and an event-driven state machine is used to structure the software. For the portable ultrasonic guided wave detection platform based on chaotic oscillator system built by external hardware devices, it can realize the precise control of the software for the instrument, realize the excitation and reception of signal, interception, chaotic detection, phase track diagram display and defect location, and propose a dichotomy method of signal to locate defects. The experiment of defect detection based on Duffing chaotic oscillator system was conducted on a 1mm thick steel pipe to verify the feasibility of this software.

articleTitle: Design and Simulations on a Novel Annular Vibration Isolator Utilizing Piezoelectric Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Vibration control of annular structures is a subject of significant research interest due to its applications in aerospace structures, gears, vehicle axles, and rotating motors. At present, passive and semi-active vibration isolation techniques are predominantly employed to address vibration control in such annular structures. However, these methods face limitations in achieving high-precision control in the low-frequency range. To overcome this limitation, this study presents the design of a novel annular vibration isolator device utilizing piezoelectric actuators, developed to meet the stringent requirements for efficient vibration isolation in annular structures. Static and dynamic simulation analyses verify the isolator's effectiveness in mitigating radial disturbances within the 100-500 Hz frequency range. The results indicate that the radial amplitude attenuation of the device can reach up to 90%.

articleTitle: Lamb Wave Characteristics In Functionally Graded One-Dimensional Hexagonal Piezoelectric Quasi-Crystal Couple-Stress Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: By considering the interaction of piezoelectric effect and couple-stress effect, the Lamb wave characteristics in functionally graded one-dimensional hexagonal piezoelectric quasi-crystal nanoplates are studied by using the Legendre orthogonal polynomial method. The interaction influences of the piezoelectric, couple-stress, and gradient effects are calculated. The piezoelectric and the couple-stress effects are mutually inhibitory. The gradient effect overall enhances the couple-stress effect of phonon modes, but weakens that of phason modes. These results can be used as a theoretical reference for the design of nano quasi-crystal structures.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Electromechanical Impedance on the Health Monitoring of Cantilever Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents a method for the online monitoring of damage in cantilever structures using Electro-Mechanical Impedance (EMI). This approach enables the assessment and early warning of the structural health state, effectively preventing accidents and reducing long-term maintenance costs. The EMI method serves as an effective technique for extracting resonance frequency information from the structure. Moreover, it assesses the health state by comparing the electromechanical impedance response signals before and after damage occurs, making it significant for the safe operation of the structure. Changes in the state of the cantilever structure affect both the conductance and susceptance components of the admittance characteristics. Based on this relationship, this study quantifies the sensitivity of the real and imaginary parts of the admittance to cantilever structure damage through a combination of simulation and experimentation. The results indicate that the real part of the admittance is more sensitive to crack damage in cantilever beams, making it more suitable for structural health monitoring. Finally, this paper employs a One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) to rapidly quantify the degree of crack damage in cantilever beams.

articleTitle: 2D Acoustofluidic Patterns Generated in Quasi-Sierpinski-Carpet Shaped Chambers with Different Radiation Surface Distributions
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Accurate, rapid, and stable control of the motion of micro- and nanoscale objects is crucial in biomedical research, compositional analysis, targeted drug delivery, and other fields. This paper proposes a strategy for generating diverse sound and flow fields in Sierpinski-type chambers, and conducts simulation research for patterned manipulation of micro-scale particles. Plenty of splendid acoustofluidic patterns can be obtained in the originally-static quasi-Sierpinski-carpet shaped chambers generated at different levels of recursion without complicated parameter modulation.The initial findings suggest the potential use of Sierpinski-type fractal structures as adaptable elements to tailor acoustofluidic fields. This customization allows for exploring topographical manipulation of biological samples and orientational control of micro/nano-scale machines beyond conventional methods.

articleTitle: Driving Circuit Design with Pulse-Width Modulation for Ultrasonic Shot Peening
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: To address the issue of resonant frequency drift in an ultrasonic shot peening system caused by heat during operation, a pulse-width modulation signal circuit has been designed using the SG3525 integrated PWM control chip. First, a voltage-controlled frequency precision adjustment method is proposed based on the source-follower principle. Furthermore, a frequency prediction formula based on the parallel total current method is derived according to the frequency modulation principle with multiple adjustable branches. Finally, an experimental platform is constructed to evaluate the frequency modulation performance under different ambient temperatures. The results demonstrate that this frequency modulation circuit effectively resolves the problem of resonant frequency drift in operation for ultrasonic shot peening transducers.

articleTitle: Molecular dynamics study on the influence of void distribution on mechanical properties of graphene-wrapped silver nanoplates with pre-existing microcracks
publicationTitle: 2024 18th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the effect of pore distribution on the mechanical properties of graphene-coated silver nanosheets with pre-existing microcracks through molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. An atomic model of the graphene-coated silver nanosheet was constructed, and uniaxial tension tensile simulations were performed under constant temperature and strain rate conditions. By analyzing the stress-strain curves and energy variation curves, the relationship between pore location and microcrack propagation was revealed. The results showed that when the pore and the microcrack tip formed a 90° angle, the system reached maximum stress, effectively inhibiting the propagation of the microcrack. In contrast, when the angle was 270°, the system exhibited minimum stress, and the inhibitory effect of the pore on microcrack propagation was significantly weakened. These findings provide new insights into understanding and optimizing the mechanical properties of nanomaterials.
